**[TERM SHEET --- CONSTRUCTION-TO-MINI-PERMANENT LOAN]{.underline}**

**The Piedmont at Brightleaf** **601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, North Carolina 27701**

**NON-BINDING EXCEPT AS SET FORTH IN SECTIONS 22 AND 23 HEREOF**

**Date:** January 10, 2025 **Bank Internal Loan Number:** CRE-2025-0342

Prepared by **Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.**, Commercial Real Estate Lending Division, 215 South Tryon Street, 18th Floor, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202.

This Term Sheet sets forth the proposed terms and conditions under which Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (\"Lender\") is prepared to provide construction-to-mini-permanent loan financing to Harborview Capital Partners LLC (\"Borrower\") for the development of the mixed-use project known as The Piedmont at Brightleaf, located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, North Carolina 27701. Except as expressly set forth in Sections 22 and 23 hereof, this Term Sheet does not constitute a binding commitment or obligation on the part of the Lender to make the proposed Loan or on the part of the Borrower to accept the proposed Loan.

**[Section 1 --- Parties]{.underline}**

**1.1 Lender. Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.**, a nationally chartered savings bank organized and existing under the laws of the United States, regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. **[Section 2 --- Project Description]{.underline}**

**Project Name:** The Piedmont at Brightleaf

**Property Address:** 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701

**Parcel IDs:** 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102

**Total Land Area:** 3.47 acres (combined two parcels)

**Zoning:** MU-D (Mixed Use --- Downtown). The proposed development is permitted as of right under the current zoning designation. No special use permit, conditional zoning, or variance is required.

**Current Condition:** Vacant improved land. The former tobacco warehouse structures on the site were demolished in August 2024. Environmental remediation of the site was completed in September 2024 in accordance with the applicable directives of the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (\"NCDEQ\").

**Development Description:** The Project consists of the ground-up construction of a six (6)-story (five residential stories over one podium level), Class A mixed-use residential and retail development, together with an associated structured parking garage. The development program is summarized as follows:

> • **Residential Unit Count:** 212 units, consisting of 142 one-bedroom units, 56 two-bedroom units, and 14 three-bedroom units
>
> • **Retail Space:** 18,400 square feet of ground-floor retail space across seven (7) retail bays
>
> • **Parking:** Four (4)-level structured parking garage with 276 spaces
>
> • **Total Gross Building Area:** 287,500 square feet
>
> • **Amenities:** Rooftop terrace, fitness center, co-working lounge, pool deck, and dog park

**General Contractor:** Graystone Construction Group Inc., 1200 Fayetteville Road, Raleigh, North Carolina 27603 (NC General Contractor License No. 78442; President: Mark D. Sullivan). The construction contract is a guaranteed maximum price (\"GMP\") contract with a GMP amount of **\$34,750,000**.

**Project Architect:** Meridian Design Collective PC, a North Carolina professional corporation.

**Projected Substantial Completion Date:** August 31, 2027.

**[Section 3 --- Loan Terms]{.underline}**

**3.1 Loan Amount**

**\$47,500,000** (Forty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand and 00/100 Dollars).

**Loan Type:** Construction-to-mini-permanent loan. The Loan shall be structured as a single advance facility, with loan proceeds to be disbursed in accordance with the approved draw schedule set forth in Section 9 of this Term Sheet.

**3.2 Loan Term**

**Construction Period:** Thirty (30) months from the date of closing. Target closing date: February 28, 2025. Construction Maturity Date: August 28, 2027.

**Mini-Perm Period:** Twelve (12) months following the Construction Maturity Date. Mini-Perm Maturity Date: August 28, 2028.

**Extension Option:** One (1) six (6)-month extension of the Mini-Perm Period (the \"Extension Option\"), resulting in an Extended Maturity Date of February 28, 2029, subject to satisfaction of customary conditions to be determined and set forth in the definitive Loan Agreement.

**3.3 Interest Rate**

**Construction Period Rate:** Daily Simple SOFR + 3.25% per annum.

**Mini-Perm Period Rate:** Daily Simple SOFR + 3.50% per annum.

**SOFR Floor:** 1.00%, applicable to both the Construction Period and the Mini-Perm Period. If Daily Simple SOFR is less than 1.00% on any applicable business day, SOFR shall be deemed to be 1.00% for purposes of calculating the interest rate applicable to such day.

**Default Rate:** The applicable contract rate plus 5.00% per annum.

Interest shall be calculated on the basis of actual days elapsed over a 360-day year. Interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall be payable monthly in arrears on the first business day of each calendar month. During the Construction Period, interest shall be funded from the Interest Reserve (as described in Section 10 hereof) until the Interest Reserve is exhausted; thereafter, interest shall be payable by the Borrower from its own funds.

\"Daily Simple SOFR\" means the Secured Overnight Financing Rate as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (or a successor administrator) for the applicable business day. Benchmark replacement provisions consistent with the Alternative Reference Rates Committee\'s recommended best practices shall be included in the definitive Loan Agreement, including customary benchmark replacement triggers, successor rate identification, and spread adjustments.

**3.4 Fees. Origination Fee:** 1.00% of the Loan Amount = **\$475,000**, payable in full at closing. The origination fee may be funded from Loan proceeds in accordance with the approved Project Budget.

**Exit Fee:**

> • 0.50% of the outstanding principal balance at the time of repayment if the Loan is repaid during the Construction Period;
>
> • 0.25% of the outstanding principal balance at the time of repayment if the Loan is repaid during the first six (6) months of the Mini-Perm Period;
>
> • No exit fee shall be payable if the Loan is repaid after the first six (6) months of the Mini-Perm Period.

**Unused Line Fee:** 0.25% per annum on the average daily undrawn commitment amount, payable quarterly in arrears, commencing on the first quarterly date following closing.

**[Section 4 --- Appraisal and Valuation]{.underline}**

An appraisal of the Property has been prepared by **Ridgeline Appraisal Services Inc.** (Appraiser: Linda M. Haverford, MAI), dated November 15, 2024, and has been reviewed by the Lender\'s internal appraisal review department. The key valuation conclusions are summarized as follows:

**[Section 6 --- Financial Covenants and Underwriting Requirements]{.underline}**

**6.1 Loan-to-Cost Ratio**

The maximum Loan-to-Cost Ratio shall not exceed **80%** of Total Project Costs at any time during the term of the Loan. For purposes of this Section 6.1, \"Total Project Costs\" means the aggregate of all costs and expenses incurred or to be incurred in connection with the acquisition, development, construction, and completion of the Project, as set forth in the approved Project Budget. As of the date hereof, Total Project Costs are estimated at \$56,700,000.

**6.2 Loan-to-Value Ratios**

The maximum Loan-to-Value Ratio on an as-completed basis shall not exceed **65%**. The maximum Loan-to-Value Ratio on an as-stabilized basis shall not exceed **65%**. The foregoing LTV ratios are based on the appraisal dated November 15, 2024 by Ridgeline Appraisal Services Inc. and are subject to reappraisal at any time at the Lender\'s discretion and at the Borrower\'s expense.

**6.3 Debt Service Coverage Ratio**

The minimum projected stabilized Debt Service Coverage Ratio shall be **1.25x**, based on interest-only debt service during the Mini-Perm Period. The DSCR shall be tested at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period and annually thereafter based on actual trailing twelve-month net operating income. If at any time the DSCR falls below 1.25x, the Borrower shall, at the Lender\'s election, either (a) make a principal curtailment sufficient to restore the DSCR to 1.25x or (b) fund a cash collateral reserve in an amount determined by the Lender.

**6.4 Borrower Net Worth**

The minimum net worth of the Borrower shall be **\$12,000,000**, tested annually. The current net worth of the Borrower is approximately \$14,200,000, based on financial statements provided to the Lender.

**6.5 Guarantor Liquidity**

The minimum combined liquidity of the Guarantors shall be **\$5,000,000**, tested quarterly. Current combined guarantor liquidity is approximately \$9,300,000, consisting of approximately \$6,100,000 attributable to Elena Vasquez-Torres and approximately \$3,200,000 attributable to Reginald K. Osei. For purposes of this requirement, \"liquidity\" means cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities readily convertible to cash within thirty (30) days.

**[Section 7 --- Guaranty]{.underline}**

**7.1 Completion Guaranty**

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver a completion guaranty (the \"Completion Guaranty\") pursuant to which each Guarantor shall jointly and severally guarantee the lien-free completion of the Project in accordance with the approved plans and specifications, the approved Project Budget, and the construction schedule, on or before the Construction Maturity Date of August 28, 2027. The Completion Guaranty shall remain in full force and effect until the Lender has received satisfactory evidence that construction of the Project has been completed in all material respects, a final certificate of occupancy has been issued by the City of Durham, and all construction liens have been released or bonded off.

**7.2 Carry Guaranty**

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver a carry guaranty (the \"Carry Guaranty\") pursuant to which each Guarantor shall jointly and severally guarantee the payment of interest and other carrying costs on the Loan during the term of the Loan. The Carry Guaranty is in addition to, and not in lieu of, the Interest Reserve described in Section 10 hereof. The Carry Guaranty shall apply to interest and carrying costs that accrue after the Interest Reserve has been exhausted or in the event that the Interest Reserve is insufficient to cover such costs.

**7.3 Partial Repayment Guaranty**

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver a partial repayment guaranty (the \"Partial Repayment Guaranty\") in the amount of **25% of the Loan Amount** (25% × \$47,500,000 = **\$11,875,000**). The Partial Repayment Guaranty shall be joint and several, meaning that each Guarantor shall be individually liable for the full guaranteed amount. The Partial Repayment Guaranty shall be subject to customary \"bad boy\" carve-out provisions, including but not limited to fraud, misrepresentation, voluntary bankruptcy, unauthorized transfer, environmental liability, and waste, which may convert the Partial Repayment Guaranty to a full recourse obligation. Specific carve-out triggers and the circumstances under which the partial recourse guaranty may be converted to full recourse shall be set forth in the definitive Loan Agreement.

**7.4 Environmental Indemnity**

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver an environmental indemnity agreement (the \"Environmental Indemnity\"), unlimited in amount, indemnifying the Lender against all environmental liabilities, losses, costs, damages, and expenses (including remediation costs, fines, penalties, and attorneys\' fees) arising out of or related to the presence, release, or threatened release of any hazardous substances on, under, or from the Property. The Environmental Indemnity shall survive the repayment of the Loan, the release or reconveyance of the Deed of Trust, and any foreclosure or deed in lieu of foreclosure.

**[Section 8 --- Collateral]{.underline}**

The Loan shall be secured by the following collateral:

> • First priority Deed of Trust on the Property (Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102; both parcels located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, North Carolina 27701), encumbering the fee simple interest in the Property, together with all improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances thereto;
>
> • First priority Assignment of Rents and Leases covering all current and future rents, revenues, and income from the Property;
>
> • First priority security interest in all personal property, fixtures, equipment, furniture, permits, plans, specifications, contracts, licenses, approvals, accounts, and general intangibles related to the Project;
>
> • Assignment of the construction contract (GMP contract with Graystone Construction Group Inc.), including all rights, claims, and benefits thereunder;
>
> • Assignment of the architect\'s contract (Meridian Design Collective PC), including all architectural plans, drawings, and specifications;
>
> • Collateral assignment of all insurance proceeds and condemnation awards related to the Property and the Project;
>
> • Pledge of 100% of membership interests in the Borrower by all members (Elena Vasquez-Torres --- 62%; Brightleaf Investors Group LLC --- 28%; Reginald K. Osei --- 10%);
>
> • Such other collateral as the Lender may reasonably require in connection with the Loan.

**[Section 9 --- Disbursement / Draw Schedule]{.underline}**

**9.1 General Disbursement Provisions**

Loan proceeds shall be disbursed in phases tied to construction milestones in accordance with the draw schedule set forth in Section 9.2 below. A **10% retainage holdback** shall apply to all hard construction cost disbursements. The retainage shall be held by the Lender and released only upon satisfaction of the conditions set forth below for Draw 9.

Each draw request submitted by the Borrower must be accompanied by: (a) an updated construction progress report prepared by the Borrower and the general contractor; (b) a third-party construction inspector\'s certification of the applicable milestone completion; (c) partial lien waivers from the general contractor and all subcontractors for work performed through the date of the draw request; (d) an updated title search or bring-down endorsement from Aldersgate Title & Escrow Inc. confirming the continued first-priority status of the Lender\'s Deed of Trust and the absence of any intervening liens; and (e) evidence that all insurance coverages required under Section 19 remain in full force and effect.

The Lender reserves the right to conduct independent inspections of the Property and the Project prior to authorizing each draw, at the Borrower\'s expense. The Lender shall use commercially reasonable efforts to process each draw request within ten (10) business days of receipt of a complete draw package.

**9.2 Draw Schedule**

  4                 Structural Frame --- Topped Out                55%                         \$6,950,000

  8                 Substantial Completion / TCO                   100%                        \$3,475,000

  9                 Retainage Release                              Post-CO                     \$3,275,000

  **Total**                                                                                    **\$47,500,000**

The retainage release (Draw 9) is subject to receipt of a final certificate of occupancy from the City of Durham and final unconditional lien waivers from the general contractor and all subcontractors.

**[Section 10 --- Interest Reserve]{.underline}**

The Lender shall fund an interest reserve of **\$4,850,000** from Loan proceeds at closing (the \"Interest Reserve\"). The Interest Reserve shall be held in a segregated sub-account of the construction loan (the \"Interest Reserve Account\") and shall be disbursed solely for the payment of interest accruing on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan during the Construction Period. Interest payments shall be made from the Interest Reserve Account on a monthly basis in accordance with the interest payment provisions set forth in Section 3.3 hereof, until such time as the Interest Reserve is exhausted.

In the event the Interest Reserve is insufficient to cover interest payments through the end of the Construction Period, the Borrower shall be obligated to fund any shortfall from its own funds within five (5) business days of written notice from the Lender. The adequacy of the Interest Reserve shall be assessed by the Lender periodically, no less than quarterly, during the Construction Period, and the Lender shall notify the Borrower of any projected deficiency.

(Commitment No. NC-2024-88712, dated December 5, 2024) and issuance of a pro forma lender\'s title insurance policy in an amount not less than the Loan Amount (\$47,500,000), insuring the Lender\'s Deed of Trust as a first-priority lien on the Property, subject only to Permitted Exceptions (as defined in Section 18 hereof);

**[Section 12 --- Representations and Warranties (Summary)]{.underline}**

The definitive Loan Agreement shall contain representations and warranties of the Borrower and the Guarantors that are customary for transactions of this type, including but not limited to the following:

> • The Borrower is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of North Carolina and has full power and authority to own the Property, conduct its business, enter into the Loan Documents, and perform all of its obligations thereunder.
>
> • The execution, delivery, and performance of the Loan Documents have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of the Borrower and its members, and the Loan Documents constitute the legal, valid, and binding obligations of the Borrower, enforceable in accordance with their respective terms.

**[Section 1: Executive Summary]{.underline}**

Harborview Capital Partners LLC (the \"Borrower\") has requested a \$47,500,000 construction-to-mini-permanent loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (the \"Bank\") for the ground-up construction of \"The Piedmont at Brightleaf,\" a 212-unit Class A mixed-use residential and retail development located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701. The subject property comprises two parcels (Parcel IDs 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102) with a combined land area of approximately 3.47 acres. The site is currently improved as vacant land, following the demolition of former tobacco warehouse structures in August 2024 and the completion of environmental remediation in September 2024.

The proposed development consists of a six-story mixed-use building with five residential floors constructed above a one-story podium containing ground-floor retail space and a four-level structured parking garage. The residential program comprises 212 units: 142 one-bedroom units, 56 two-bedroom units, and 14 three-bedroom units. Ground-floor retail consists of approximately 18,400 square feet across seven retail bays. The structured parking garage provides 276 parking spaces, representing a ratio of approximately 1.30 spaces per residential unit. Total gross building area is approximately 287,500 square feet. Project amenities include a rooftop terrace, fitness center, co-working lounge, pool deck, and dog park. The property is zoned MU-D (Mixed Use --- Downtown), and the proposed development is permitted as of right under the applicable zoning ordinance.

The Relationship Manager for this credit is David Forsythe, SVP, Commercial Real Estate Lending. A term sheet was executed on January 10, 2025 by David Forsythe on behalf of the Bank and Elena Vasquez-Torres, Managing Member of the Borrower. The target closing date is February 28, 2025. The Bank\'s outside legal counsel for this transaction is Ashford, Cromdale Consulting & Laine LLP (lead partner Katharine \"Kate\" Drummond; associate Marcus Webb), located at 411 South Tryon Street, Suite 2800, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202. The Borrower\'s counsel is Calloway & Strauss PLLC (lead partner Jonathan F. Ngo), located at 324 Blackwell Street, Suite 200, Durham, North Carolina 27701.

The Commercial Real Estate Lending group recommends **APPROVAL** of this loan, subject to material conditions including, without limitation, (a) resolution of a loan-to-cost ratio exceedance through funding of an equity escrow deposit, (b) execution of an intercreditor agreement with the mezzanine lender, (c) implementation of single-purpose entity covenants and delivery of a non-consolidation opinion, and (d) resolution of other conditions detailed in Section 10 of this memorandum. The loan as structured presents certain underwriting concerns regarding borrower equity contribution and LTC compliance that must be addressed as conditions of closing. Additionally, this credit memorandum identifies several risk factors and structural issues --- including interest reserve adequacy, affiliate relationships between a Borrower member and the mezzanine lender, conflicting membership interest pledges, environmental use restrictions, and title matters --- each of which requires resolution or mitigation before or at closing. These matters are fully analyzed in Sections 5, 6, 9, and 10 of this memorandum.

**[Section 2: Borrower / Sponsor Overview]{.underline}**

**[2.1 Borrower Entity]{.underline}**

The Borrower is Harborview Capital Partners LLC, a North Carolina limited liability company formed on March 14, 2019 and registered with the North Carolina Secretary of State under File Number 1923847. The Borrower\'s principal office is located at 400 West Main Street, Suite 310, Durham, North Carolina 27701. The Borrower was formed for the specific purpose of developing and operating The Piedmont at Brightleaf and is intended to function as a single-purpose entity (\"SPE\") in connection with the proposed financing.

The Borrower\'s current net worth, as reflected in its most recent financial statements provided to the Bank, is approximately \$14,200,000. The proposed loan documentation will include a minimum net worth covenant of \$12,000,000, to be tested annually within 120 days of the Borrower\'s fiscal year end. The current net worth provides a cushion of approximately \$2,200,000 above the covenant minimum.

The Borrower\'s principal, Elena Vasquez-Torres, and her affiliated entities have a demonstrated track record in commercial real estate development in the Research Triangle area. Prior to the formation of the Borrower, Ms. Vasquez-Torres and her development team successfully completed four mixed-use projects in the Triangle area, comprising a total of approximately 580 residential units and 65,000 square feet of commercial space, with aggregate development costs of approximately \$128 million. Each of these projects was completed on time and within budget, and all four have achieved stabilized occupancy levels consistent with or exceeding original projections.

The Bank\'s underwriting standards for construction loans require standard SPE covenants, including separateness covenants, restrictions on commingling of funds with affiliates, and prohibition on incurrence of additional indebtedness outside the approved capital structure. Given the affiliate relationship between a Borrower member (Brightleaf Investors Group LLC) and the mezzanine lender (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC), outside counsel should evaluate whether an independent manager requirement and/or a non-consolidation opinion should be required. This is discussed further in Section 9 (Risk Factors). The Borrower\'s operating agreement will need to be amended prior to closing to incorporate the required SPE provisions and the independent manager requirement, and the Bank\'s counsel should review the amended operating agreement to confirm compliance with the Bank\'s standard form and requirements.

**[2.2 Membership / Organizational Structure]{.underline}**

The Borrower\'s membership structure, as set forth in its operating agreement dated March 14, 2019 (as amended), is as follows:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Member**                       **Membership Interest**   **Role**
  -------------------------------- ------------------------- -----------------------
  Elena Vasquez-Torres             62%                       Managing Member

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Elena Vasquez-Torres** serves as the Managing Member of the Borrower and has day-to-day management authority over all operations of the Borrower and the Project pursuant to the operating agreement. Ms. Vasquez-Torres has the authority to execute contracts, manage development activities, and conduct the ordinary business affairs of the Borrower without the consent of the other members. Major decisions --- including the incurrence of indebtedness, sale or disposition of the Project, refinancing of existing debt, and any voluntary filing for bankruptcy or insolvency protection --- require the affirmative approval of members holding at least 75% of the outstanding membership interests.

**Brightleaf Investors Group LLC** is a North Carolina limited liability company (NC Secretary of State File No. 2045612) that serves as the investment vehicle for a group of local high-net-worth investors. Its Managing Member is Thomas R. Chen. Notably, Thomas R. Chen also controls Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC (NC Secretary of State File No. 2103988), the entity providing the \$9,200,000 mezzanine loan for the Project. These two entities --- Brightleaf Investors Group LLC and Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC --- share common control through Mr. Chen, creating a structural affiliate relationship that is discussed extensively in Sections 4.4 and 9.3 of this memorandum. This common control raises concerns regarding the independence of the mezzanine financing from the Borrower\'s equity structure and introduces substantive consolidation risk that must be addressed through appropriate SPE covenants, independent manager provisions, and a non-consolidation opinion.

**[3.2 Market Overview]{.underline}**

The Durham, North Carolina multifamily market continues to demonstrate strong fundamentals driven by the area\'s robust economic base. The Research Triangle region --- anchored by Duke University, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and North Carolina State University --- has attracted significant investment in biotechnology, pharmaceutical research, information technology, and financial services. Downtown Durham, in particular, has experienced substantial revitalization over the past decade, with the American Tobacco Campus, Durham Innovation District, and the expanding Duke University Health System serving as major employment and demand drivers. Population growth in Durham County has averaged approximately 1.8% annually over the past five years, and the median household income in the downtown core has increased by over 15% during the same period.

Average market rents for Class A multifamily product in downtown Durham currently range from approximately \$1,950 to \$2,500 per month for one-bedroom units and \$2,300 to \$3,200 per month for two-bedroom units, depending on unit size, finishes, and amenity package. The Project\'s projected average rent of \$2,245 per month across all unit types is positioned in the mid-range of the competitive set and is supported by comparable lease data from properties including the Van Alen, One City Center Apartments, and Beckon on Geer Street. The Bank considers this rent projection to be reasonable and achievable based on current market conditions.

Ground-floor retail rents in downtown Durham for Class A mixed-use buildings with street-level visibility range from approximately \$26.00 to \$35.00 per square foot on a triple-net basis. The projected retail rent of \$30.00 per square foot NNN is within this market range and is considered reasonable given the Project\'s location and visibility along Foster Street.

Durham Class A multifamily vacancy rates have historically ranged from approximately 4% to 7%, with the most recent data indicating a vacancy rate of approximately 5.2% for comparable properties. The Project\'s underwritten vacancy assumption of 5% is consistent with historical trends and is considered appropriate. While there is a notable pipeline of competing multifamily projects under development or planned in the greater Durham area, market demand continues to absorb new supply at a rate that supports the Project\'s lease-up assumptions. The Bank\'s independent market assessment supports the appraised values discussed in Section 3.3.

**The Borrower is contributing \$0 in direct cash equity to the Project.** The land acquisition cost of \$8,200,000 was funded from prior capital calls from members, including contributions from Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, which is affiliated with the mezzanine lender, Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC. All remaining project costs are funded through the senior construction loan and the mezzanine loan. Per the Bank\'s underwriting policy, mezzanine debt is not counted as borrower equity.

The LTC calculation presents a compliance issue. Total project costs equal \$56,700,000. The senior loan amount is \$47,500,000. Therefore, LTC = \$47,500,000 ÷ \$56,700,000 = **83.77%**. The Bank\'s maximum permitted LTC per the executed term sheet and per the Bank\'s Commercial Real Estate Lending Policy is 80%. At the maximum LTC of 80%, the maximum permitted senior loan amount would be \$56,700,000 × 80% = \$45,360,000. The proposed loan amount of \$47,500,000 exceeds this maximum by \$2,140,000. This discrepancy must be resolved prior to closing through the equity escrow mechanism described in Section 5.3 and conditioned in Section 10.

Additionally, the Bank notes that the Borrower\'s only equity contribution to the Project is the previously acquired land, which has an as-is appraised value of \$8,900,000 and was acquired for \$8,200,000. While the land value exceeds the \$2,140,000 shortfall, a portion of the capital used to acquire the land was sourced from Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, an affiliate of the mezzanine lender. This creates a potential circular funding concern. The Senior Loan Committee requires, as a condition of closing, that the Borrower either: (a) deposit \$2,140,000 in cash into a Bank-controlled equity escrow account prior to closing; or (b) reduce the loan amount to \$45,360,000; or (c) provide additional evidence satisfactory to the Bank that the land equity is independent of the mezzanine financing.

The loan-to-cost ratio is a critical underwriting metric that measures the Bank\'s exposure relative to total project costs. The detailed LTC calculation is as follows:

The LTC ratio of 83.77% exceeds the Bank\'s maximum of 80% as stated in the term sheet. The term sheet was executed with a loan amount of \$47,500,000 and total project costs of \$56,700,000 without reconciling the LTC covenant. This discrepancy must be resolved prior to closing. The Senior Loan Committee acknowledges the LTC exceedance and approves the loan subject to the condition that the Borrower fund an equity escrow deposit of not less than \$2,140,000 in cash (from sources other than the mezzanine loan or any affiliate of the mezzanine lender) into a Bank-controlled escrow account prior to or at closing. This equity escrow will be applied to project costs first, ahead of loan advances, to bring the effective LTC into compliance.

For additional context, the Bank notes the following alternative analysis: If the mezzanine debt of \$9,200,000 were hypothetically counted as equity (which the Bank\'s underwriting policy does not permit), the combined \"equity\" in the capital structure would be \$9,200,000 and the senior loan LTC would remain unchanged at 83.77%. The combined senior and mezzanine leverage is (\$47,500,000 + \$9,200,000) ÷ \$56,700,000 = 100%, meaning there is zero true equity cushion in the capital structure absent the land value. This analysis underscores the importance of the equity escrow requirement and the need for the Bank to confirm that the land equity is genuinely independent of the mezzanine financing.

Even with the proposed equity escrow of \$2,140,000, the Borrower\'s total equity contribution to the Project would consist of \$2,140,000 in cash plus \$8,200,000 in land (at cost), totaling \$10,340,000 out of \$56,700,000 in total project costs, or approximately 18.2%. While this level of equity is relatively thin for a ground-up construction loan, the Bank takes comfort in the strong LTV ratios (65.25% as-completed, 62.34% as-stabilized) and the combined guarantor net worth of \$41,300,000 as additional credit support.

Assuming a Daily Simple SOFR rate of 4.35% (as of the credit memo date) plus the mini-perm spread of 3.50%, the all-in rate is 7.85%. Annual interest on \$47,500,000 at 7.85% = \$3,728,750. DSCR = \$4,876,800 ÷ \$3,728,750 = **1.31x**, which exceeds the Bank\'s minimum of 1.25x.

**Stress-Tested DSCR.** Under a stress scenario assuming a 200-basis-point increase in SOFR (to 6.35%), the all-in mini-perm rate would be 9.85% (6.35% + 3.50%). Annual interest on \$47,500,000 at 9.85% = \$4,678,750. Stressed DSCR = \$4,876,800 ÷ \$4,678,750 = **1.04x**, which falls below the Bank\'s minimum of 1.25x. This stress test illustrates the loan\'s sensitivity to interest rate increases and underscores the importance of the Borrower securing permanent take-out financing or obtaining an interest rate cap prior to the commencement of the mini-perm period or any extension thereof. The Bank should consider requiring an interest rate cap as a condition of the extension option.

**[6.2 Interest Reserve Analysis]{.underline}**

The interest reserve of \$4,850,000 is funded from loan proceeds at closing and held in a designated sub-account to cover monthly interest payments during the construction period. The adequacy of this reserve is a critical underwriting consideration, as depletion of the reserve before construction completion would require the Borrower to fund interest from its own resources.

**Current Rate Assumptions.** The current Daily Simple SOFR rate is approximately 4.35% as of the date of this memorandum. The construction period all-in rate is Daily Simple SOFR + 3.25% = 7.60%.

**Full-Draw Scenario.** If the entire \$47,500,000 were drawn immediately at closing, the annual interest expense would be \$47,500,000 × 7.60% = \$3,610,000. Over the 30-month construction period, total interest cost would be approximately \$3,610,000 × (30 ÷ 12) = \$9,025,000. However, this scenario is unrealistic because the loan is drawn incrementally over the construction period based on milestone achievements.

**Incremental Draw Scenario.** Based on the draw schedule (Section 7.1), the loan is drawn progressively as construction milestones are achieved. Draw 1 at closing (\$9,475,000) represents approximately 20% of the total loan commitment. Subsequent draws bring cumulative outstanding balances to progressively higher levels, with Draw 8 (substantial completion) bringing cumulative draws to approximately \$44,225,000 and the final Draw 9 (retainage release) occurring post-certificate of occupancy. Assuming a roughly linear draw pattern over approximately 18 months to reach the full commitment level (with the remaining 12 months of the construction period at or near full draw), the average outstanding balance over the 30-month construction period is estimated at approximately \$28,500,000 (roughly 60% of \$47,500,000).

Using this average balance, the estimated total interest cost during the 30-month construction period is: \$28,500,000 × 7.60% × (30 ÷ 12) = approximately **\$5,415,000**.

The interest reserve of \$4,850,000 is therefore approximately **\$565,000 short** of the estimated total interest cost under current rate assumptions.

**Sensitivity Analysis.** If SOFR increases by 100 basis points to 5.35%, the all-in construction rate would be 8.60%. Estimated total interest cost would increase to \$28,500,000 × 8.60% × (30 ÷ 12) = approximately **\$6,128,000**, creating a potential shortfall of approximately \$1,278,000.

Furthermore, the draw schedule is somewhat front-loaded, with the initial closing draw of \$9,475,000 representing approximately 20% of the total commitment. This front-loading means the average outstanding balance may be higher than the linear assumption suggests, potentially increasing the total interest cost and widening the reserve shortfall.

**Assessment.** The interest reserve of \$4,850,000 is **tight** under current rate assumptions and would be clearly inadequate in a rising rate environment. The Senior Loan Committee approves the interest reserve of \$4,850,000 as adequate based on current rate assumptions, but notes that this amount is at the lower boundary of adequacy. The loan documentation must include the following protective provisions:

> • A mandatory borrower replenishment obligation requiring the Borrower to fund any interest reserve shortfall from its own funds (not from loan proceeds or mezzanine loan proceeds) upon demand by the Bank.
>
> • An interest reserve adequacy test to be performed at each draw request, comparing the remaining interest reserve balance against projected interest costs through the earlier of (a) the next anticipated draw date or (b) 90 days. If the projected costs exceed the remaining reserve balance, the Borrower must deposit additional funds into the interest reserve sub-account before the requested advance will be funded.
>
> • A reporting obligation requiring the Borrower to provide the Bank with a monthly reconciliation of the interest reserve balance, actual interest charges, and projected remaining interest costs through construction maturity.

**[6.3 Projected Stabilized Cash Flow]{.underline}**

The Bank has independently verified the appraiser\'s projected stabilized net operating income by reviewing comparable market data, lease comparables, and operating expense benchmarks for Class A mixed-use properties in the Durham market. **[Section 9: Risk Factors and Mitigants]{.underline}**

**[9.1 Risk Factor: LTC Ratio Exceedance and Zero Cash Equity]{.underline}**

**Risk.** The loan-to-cost ratio of 83.77% exceeds the Bank\'s maximum permitted LTC of 80% as set forth in both the executed term sheet and the Bank\'s Commercial Real Estate Lending Policy. The Borrower is contributing zero dollars (\$0) in direct cash equity to the Project. The only equity in the capital stack is the previously acquired land, which has an as-is appraised value of \$8,900,000 and was acquired for \$8,200,000. A portion of the capital used to fund the land acquisition was sourced from Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, an affiliate of the mezzanine lender, Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC. The combined senior loan and mezzanine loan totals \$56,700,000, which equals 100% of total project costs, resulting in zero true equity cushion beyond the embedded value in the land.

**Impact.** The Bank has an outsized exposure relative to total project costs. In a default scenario, the Bank\'s recovery would depend entirely on the collateral value of the Project and the guarantor resources. The absence of any cash equity contribution means the Borrower has limited \"skin in the game\" from a cash perspective, which increases moral hazard risk --- the risk that the Borrower may be less motivated to resolve problems or fund cost overruns if the Borrower has no cash at risk. The 100% combined leverage ratio means that any decline in project value below total development costs would result in a loss position for one or both lenders, with the senior lender bearing the risk of value declines below the \$47,500,000 senior loan balance.

**Mitigants.** (a) The Bank will require the Borrower to deposit \$2,140,000 in cash into a Bank-controlled equity escrow account prior to closing, which will be disbursed ahead of loan advances to fund project costs and bring the effective LTC into compliance with the 80% maximum. (b) The land has an appraised value of \$8,900,000, which is \$700,000 above the acquisition cost, providing embedded equity. (c) The LTV ratios are well within the Bank\'s policy limits (65.25% as-completed, 62.34% as-stabilized), indicating adequate value coverage. (d) The combined guarantor net worth of \$41,300,000 provides substantial credit support beyond the collateral. (e) The completion and carry guarantees obligate the guarantors to fund cost overruns and cover carrying costs, providing protection against construction budget and timeline risks.

**Residual Concern.** Even with the equity escrow, the Borrower\'s total equity contribution would be only \$2,140,000 in cash plus \$8,200,000 in land (at cost) = \$10,340,000 out of \$56,700,000 in total project costs = approximately 18.2%. This is relatively thin for a ground-up construction loan, where the Bank\'s policy guidance generally targets borrower equity contributions of 20% or more. However, the strong LTV position and guarantor support mitigate this concern to an acceptable level.

**[9.2 Risk Factor: Interest Reserve Adequacy]{.underline}**

**Risk.** As analyzed in Section 6.2, the \$4,850,000 interest reserve funded from loan proceeds at closing may be insufficient by approximately \$565,000 under current rate assumptions and a reasonable incremental draw assumption. If SOFR increases by 100 basis points, the estimated shortfall would widen to approximately \$1,278,000.

**Impact.** If the interest reserve is depleted before construction completion, the Borrower must fund monthly interest payments from its own resources. Given the Borrower\'s zero cash equity contribution, the Borrower may lack immediate liquidity to fund interest shortfalls, potentially creating a payment default during the construction period. A payment default during construction could trigger cross-defaults under the mezzanine loan and could jeopardize the construction timeline if the Bank suspends further advances.

**Mitigants.** (a) The loan documentation will include a mandatory borrower replenishment obligation requiring the Borrower to fund any interest reserve shortfall from its own funds upon demand by the Bank. (b) Interest reserve adequacy will be tested at each draw request, with the Borrower required to replenish the reserve if projected remaining interest costs during the construction period exceed the remaining reserve balance. (c) The guarantors maintain combined liquidity of \$9,300,000, which provides a backstop for interest reserve replenishment. (d) The interest reserve analysis assumes a current SOFR of approximately 4.35%. If SOFR rates decline during the construction period, the reserve could prove adequate or even generate a surplus.

**Recommendation.** The Senior Loan Committee approves the \$4,850,000 interest reserve as adequate based on current rate assumptions, with mandatory contractual protections as described above. The Bank should monitor SOFR rate trends closely and communicate proactively with the Borrower regarding any anticipated replenishment obligations.

**[9.3 Risk Factor: Mezzanine Lender Affiliate Relationship and SPE Concerns]{.underline}**

**Risk.** Brightleaf Investors Group LLC (28% member of the Borrower) shares common control with Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC (mezzanine lender) through Thomas R. Chen. This common control creates a structural conflict and raises the following specific concerns:

First, the mezzanine lender is providing \$9,200,000 in subordinated debt to a borrower in which its affiliate holds a significant (28%) equity interest. This interrelationship blurs the distinction between debt and equity in the Borrower\'s capital structure and may complicate the enforcement of remedies in a default or insolvency scenario.

Second, the affiliate relationship increases **substantive consolidation risk**. In a bankruptcy proceeding involving the Borrower, a court could potentially substantively consolidate the assets and liabilities of the Borrower with those of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, or other entities under common control with Thomas R. Chen. Substantive consolidation would merge the separate estates into a single bankruptcy estate, potentially subordinating the Bank\'s claims, complicating the Bank\'s realization upon its collateral, or exposing the collateral to the claims of creditors of the affiliated entities.

Third, the Borrower\'s intended status as a single-purpose entity requires strict separateness from its members and their affiliates. Standard SPE covenants mandate separate books and records, no commingling of funds, arm\'s-length transactions, separate corporate formalities, and restrictions on affiliate dealings. The affiliate structure between a Borrower member and the mezzanine lender creates inherent tension with these separateness requirements.

**Impact.** If SPE covenants are inadequate or are not faithfully observed, the Bank\'s collateral position could be compromised in a bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding involving the Borrower or any affiliated entity. The risk of substantive consolidation, while relatively uncommon in practice, is heightened in situations where affiliated entities have overlapping ownership, shared management, commingled funds, or inadequate corporate formalities.

**Mitigants.** The Bank requires the following protective measures as conditions of closing:

\(a\) **Robust SPE Covenants.** The loan agreement must include comprehensive SPE covenants requiring the Borrower to: maintain its existence as a separate legal entity; maintain separate books, records, and bank accounts; conduct all transactions with affiliates on arm\'s-length terms; refrain from commingling its assets or funds with those of any member, affiliate, or other person; observe all limited liability company formalities; hold itself out as an entity separate and distinct from its members and their affiliates; and pay its own liabilities and expenses from its own funds.

\(b\) **Independent Manager.** The Borrower\'s operating agreement must be amended to require the appointment of at least one independent manager (who is not an officer, director, employee, or affiliate of the Borrower, any member, or the mezzanine lender) whose affirmative vote is required for any voluntary filing for bankruptcy, reorganization, or insolvency protection. This provision is the single most important structural safeguard against a bad-faith bankruptcy filing.

\(c\) **Non-Consolidation Opinion.** Borrower\'s counsel (Calloway & Strauss PLLC) must deliver, at closing, a non-consolidation opinion addressed to the Bank, opining that, subject to customary assumptions and qualifications, a court applying applicable North Carolina law would not substantively consolidate the Borrower with any of its members, affiliates, or other related entities. This opinion provides additional assurance (though not a guarantee) that the Borrower\'s separate existence will be respected in a judicial proceeding.

\(d\) **Intercreditor Provisions.** The intercreditor agreement must include express acknowledgments of the affiliate relationship and provisions prohibiting the mezzanine lender from filing or joining in the filing of an involuntary bankruptcy petition against the Borrower.

**Market Standard.** For securitization-eligible construction loans, industry-standard SPE requirements include independent director or independent manager provisions and non-consolidation opinions from borrower\'s counsel. While this loan is not currently intended for securitization, implementing these protections is prudent given the heightened affiliate risk. The analytical framework for non-consolidation analysis draws on Delaware LLC law principles (even though the Borrower is a North Carolina LLC), as the Delaware case law provides the most developed body of precedent on substantive consolidation in the context of structured finance transactions.

**[9.4 Risk Factor: Conflicting Membership Interest Pledges]{.underline}**

**Risk.** Both the senior construction loan and the mezzanine loan are secured by a pledge of 100% of the membership interests in the Borrower. As a matter of law and commercial practice, only one lender can hold a first-priority security interest in the same collateral. As currently documented, the pledges are mutually exclusive as first-priority interests, creating an ambiguity that could result in litigation or contested priority in a default scenario.

**Impact.** If the conflicting pledges are not resolved, the Bank may not have the collateral position described in the term sheet. In a default, the mezzanine lender could assert a competing first-priority claim to the membership interests, and the resulting dispute could delay or prevent the Bank\'s exercise of remedies, including foreclosure on the membership interests or exercise of control over the Borrower.

**Mitigants.** Execution of the intercreditor agreement (currently negotiated but not yet executed) must be a condition precedent to closing. The intercreditor agreement must provide: (i) the senior lender (Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.) holds a first-priority security interest in both the real property collateral and the membership interests; (ii) the mezzanine lender (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC) holds a subordinated second-priority security interest in the membership interests; (iii) the mezzanine lender is subject to a 90-day standstill period before exercising any remedies; (iv) the mezzanine lender has cure rights and a purchase option (right to acquire the senior loan at par plus accrued); and (v) the mezzanine lender may not modify the terms of the mezzanine loan without the Bank\'s prior written consent.

**Alternative.** If the intercreditor agreement cannot be finalized on terms satisfactory to the Bank, the Bank could forego the membership interest pledge and rely solely on its real property collateral (first-priority deed of trust, assignment of rents and leases, security interest in personal property). The LTV ratios support the real property collateral alone. However, the membership interest pledge provides an additional layer of protection and operational control that the Bank considers valuable, particularly in a construction loan context where the Bank needs the ability to step in and control the development entity if the Borrower defaults.

**Recommendation.** The Bank requires execution of the intercreditor agreement as a hard closing condition. The loan may not close without a fully executed and delivered intercreditor agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank and its counsel.

**[9.5 Risk Factor: Environmental Use Restriction / Residential Conflict]{.underline}**

**Risk.** The NFA letter issued by NCDEQ on September 30, 2024 restricts the approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 to non-residential use. However, the current project plans position 14 residential units in the building structure directly above this area at the podium level and upper floors.

**Impact.** If this conflict is not resolved, those 14 units may not receive residential certificates of occupancy from the City of Durham, which would reduce the Project\'s rental income and adversely affect the Bank\'s underwriting assumptions. The estimated annual revenue impact of losing 14 residential units is approximately \$377,160 (14 units × \$2,245 average monthly rent × 12 months). This would reduce the stabilized NOI to approximately \$4,499,640 (\$4,876,800 − \$377,160), and the recalculated DSCR would be approximately \$4,499,640 ÷ \$3,728,750 = 1.21x, which is below the Bank\'s minimum of 1.25x. Additionally, the as-completed and as-stabilized appraised values may be overstated if they assume occupancy and income from the affected 14 units without accounting for the use restriction.

**Mitigants.** The Bank requires the Borrower, as a condition of closing (or, at the Bank\'s discretion, as a condition precedent to advances for construction above the podium level in the affected area), to achieve one of the following resolutions: (a) obtain a modification to the NFA letter from NCDEQ permitting residential use of the area, contingent on installation and ongoing maintenance of the soil vapor mitigation system; (b) redesign the 14 affected units as commercial or retail space and provide updated financial projections; or (c) provide written confirmation from NCDEQ that residential use is permitted in the floors above the grade-level restricted area, provided that appropriate engineering controls (including the vapor mitigation system) are in place and operational.

**Recommendation.** The Bank flags this issue for review by outside counsel and environmental consultants. The resolution approach should be documented as a specific covenant in the loan documentation, and the Bank should retain discretion to withhold advances for construction in the affected area until the issue is resolved to the Bank\'s satisfaction.

**Risk.** The 30-month construction period targets projected substantial completion on August 31, 2027. The construction maturity date under the loan is August 28, 2027 --- only three days before the projected substantial completion date. **Market Risk.** The Durham multifamily market is currently strong, but the 30-month construction horizon introduces inherent uncertainty regarding supply, demand, and rental rate trends. The 5% vacancy assumption is adequate based on historical trends, and the Bank considers the risk of a significant market downturn during the construction period to be moderate but not negligible. The Bank will monitor market conditions throughout the construction period and may require updated market studies as a condition of the extension option.

The city\'s economic base is anchored by major employers including Duke University, the Duke University Health System, IBM, Hartleigh Investments, and numerous biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies clustered in and around Research Triangle Park.

Downtown Durham, in particular, has undergone significant revitalization over the past fifteen years, with substantial public and private investment transforming the American Tobacco, Brightleaf, and West Village districts into vibrant mixed-use neighborhoods. The redevelopment of historic tobacco warehouses and surrounding properties has attracted a critical mass of residential, retail, restaurant, and entertainment uses that have established downtown Durham as one of the most desirable urban neighborhoods in the Research Triangle region.

**[Section 5 --- Highest and Best Use Analysis]{.underline}**

**[As Vacant]{.underline}**

The highest and best use of the subject property, as if vacant and available for development, was analyzed in accordance with the four standard tests: legal permissibility, physical possibility, financial feasibility, and maximum productivity. The site\'s MU-D zoning permits a range of uses including residential, retail, office, hotel, and mixed-use development, all by right, with structures up to 120 feet in height. The site\'s physical characteristics --- including its 3.47-acre size, generally level topography, availability of all municipal utilities, and favorable street frontage --- support a variety of development programs. Alternative uses considered in the analysis included office development, hotel development, and exclusively retail development. Each alternative was evaluated against a mixed-use residential and retail program. Based on the land residual analysis performed in the full appraisal report, a mixed-use residential and retail development of the type and scale proposed for the subject was determined to produce the highest land residual value and is therefore concluded to represent the highest and best use of the land as if vacant.

**[As Proposed (Improved)]{.underline}**

The highest and best use of the property as proposed --- that is, assuming construction of the 212-unit mixed-use residential and retail development as described in Section 3 --- satisfies all four tests. The proposed development is legally permissible under MU-D zoning without the need for variances or special permits. It is physically possible given the site\'s dimensions, topography, and infrastructure availability. It is financially feasible based on the income projections and cost analysis set forth in this report, which indicate that the prospective stabilized net operating income will support a market value in excess of the total development cost. Finally, the proposed development is maximally productive relative to alternative development programs analyzed by the appraiser, as it generates the highest return on cost among the programs considered.

**[Conclusion]{.underline}**

The proposed development of The Piedmont at Brightleaf --- a 212-unit Class A mixed-use residential and retail project --- represents the highest and best use of the subject property, both as if vacant and as proposed.

**[Section 6 --- Valuation Methodology and Conclusions]{.underline}**

**[Section 6.1 --- As-Is Land Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approach:** The as-is market value of the subject land was estimated using the sales comparison approach, which is the most reliable and widely accepted methodology for valuing vacant land in an active market with sufficient comparable data. The subject is valued in its current condition as of the effective date: vacant, cleared, and rough-graded, with environmental remediation completed and all municipal utilities available.

**Comparable Land Sales:** The appraiser identified and analyzed four recent sales of comparable development land in the downtown Durham and adjacent urban submarkets. Each comparable was adjusted for differences in location, size, shape, access, utilities, topography, and market conditions (time of sale). The comparable sales and adjustments are summarized below:

**Sale 1:** A 2.81-acre parcel located on West Chapel Hill Street, Durham, sold in July 2024 for \$7,447,000, or \$2,650,000 per acre. The parcel is zoned for mixed-use development and is located approximately 0.5 miles west of the subject. After adjustment for the subject\'s superior street frontage and slightly less favorable vehicular access from a secondary roadway, the adjusted rate is \$2,510,000 per acre.

**Sale 2:** A 1.95-acre parcel located on Morris Street, Durham, sold in April 2024 for \$5,460,000, or \$2,800,000 per acre. The parcel is smaller than the subject and has a more regular shape, which typically commands a premium on a per-acre basis for efficient development. After adjustment for the subject\'s larger size and irregular configuration, the adjusted rate is \$2,620,000 per acre.

**Sale 3:** A 4.12-acre parcel located on Mangum Street, Durham, sold in January 2024 for \$9,888,000, or \$2,400,000 per acre. The parcel is located in a transitional area approximately 0.7 miles north of the downtown core and was adjusted upward for the subject\'s superior Brightleaf district location and proximity to established amenities. The adjusted rate is \$2,550,000 per acre.

**Sale 4:** A 3.05-acre assemblage of two parcels located on Corporation Street, Durham, sold in September 2023 for \$7,168,000, or \$2,350,000 per acre. The sale occurred approximately 14 months prior to the effective date and was adjusted upward for market conditions (positive price trend in downtown Durham land values) and for the subject\'s superior frontage and access. The adjusted rate is \$2,480,000 per acre.

**Indicated Value Range:** The adjusted comparable sales indicate a range of \$2,480,000 to \$2,620,000 per acre for the subject land.

**Selected Rate:** After reconciliation of the comparable data, placing greatest weight on Sales 1 and 3 as most similar in size and location to the subject, the appraiser selected a rate of approximately \$2,565,000 per acre.

**As-Is Land Value:** 3.47 acres × \$2,565,000 per acre = \$8,900,550, rounded to **\$8,900,000**.

**Reconciliation:** The concluded as-is land value of \$8,900,000 is consistent with the land acquisition cost of \$8,200,000, which was the price paid by Harborview Capital Partners LLC in early 2024 prior to the demolition of the existing warehouse structures and the completion of environmental remediation. The demolition and remediation activities, which cost approximately \$680,000, have contributed to the current enhanced value of the land in its cleared and development-ready condition.

**[Section 6.2 --- As-Completed Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approaches Used:** The as-completed market value of the subject property was estimated using the income capitalization approach as the primary valuation methodology, supported by the sales comparison approach as a secondary check on reasonableness.

**Income Capitalization Approach**

The \"as-completed\" value reflects the market value of the proposed development upon completion of construction but prior to the achievement of stabilized occupancy. This valuation scenario recognizes that, at the point of construction completion, the property will not yet have reached its projected stabilized occupancy of 95% and the owner will incur costs and experience income loss during the lease-up period. Accordingly, the as-completed value is derived by deducting from the as-stabilized value the estimated costs and economic impact of the lease-up period.

The prospective stabilized net operating income (\"NOI\") of the subject, as detailed in Section 7 below, is \$4,876,800 per annum. Applied at the selected capitalization rate of 6.40%, the indicated as-stabilized value is \$76,200,000 (see Section 6.3 below).

**Lease-Up Deductions from As-Stabilized Value:**

The appraiser estimated the following deductions to account for the lease-up period between construction completion and stabilization:

> • **Estimated lease-up period:** 9 months (midpoint of the 8- to 10-month range projected in Section 4), commencing upon receipt of the certificate of occupancy.
>
> • **Lost rental income during lease-up:** Assuming a linear absorption from 0% to 95% occupancy over the 9-month period, the effective average occupancy during lease-up is approximately 47.5%. The resulting lost rental income relative to stabilized occupancy (95%) is estimated at approximately \$2,450,000.
>
> • **Lease-up costs:** Additional marketing expenditures, concessions to early tenants (estimated at an average of one month\'s free rent per unit), and supplemental on-site leasing staff are estimated to total approximately \$680,000.
>
> • **Total lease-up adjustment:** Approximately \$3,130,000.
>
> • **Discount for lease-up risk and timing:** An additional deduction of approximately \$270,000 is applied to account for the risk and present-value discount associated with the timing uncertainty of the lease-up period.
>
> • **Total deduction from as-stabilized value:** \$3,130,000 + \$270,000 = \$3,400,000.

**As-Completed Value via Income Approach:** \$76,200,000 − \$3,400,000 = **\$72,800,000**.

**Sales Comparison Approach (Supportive)**

As a supportive check on the income capitalization approach, the appraiser analyzed three comparable sales of recently constructed mixed-use multifamily properties in the Research Triangle area. The sales indicated a price range of \$330,000 to \$360,000 per residential unit, after adjustment for the retail component. Applied to the subject\'s 212 residential units, the midpoint of approximately \$343,000 per unit indicates a value of approximately \$72,700,000, which is highly supportive of the income approach conclusion.

**Concluded As-Completed Market Value: \$72,800,000**

**[Section 6.3 --- As-Stabilized Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approach:** The as-stabilized market value was estimated using the income capitalization approach, specifically the direct capitalization method.

**Stabilization Assumption:** Stabilized occupancy is defined as 95% across all residential units and retail bays, consistent with the observed stabilized occupancy levels at the comparable properties in the downtown Durham submarket.

**Projected Stabilization Date:** The appraiser projects that the subject will achieve stabilized occupancy approximately nine months following projected substantial completion, or approximately May 2028.

**Capitalization Rate Analysis:** The overall capitalization rate was derived from an analysis of five comparable property sales in the Raleigh-Durham metropolitan market, all involving Class A multifamily or mixed-use residential properties with recent construction dates. The observed capitalization rates for these transactions ranged from 5.75% to 7.10%, with a mean of approximately 6.35% and a median of approximately 6.40%. The variance in observed rates reflects differences in property quality, location, tenant profile, and the proportion of retail versus residential income.

**Selected Capitalization Rate: 6.40%.** The selected rate is positioned at the median of the comparable range and reflects the subject\'s status as a new-construction, Class A property in a prime downtown location with strong demand fundamentals. The rate also accounts for the current interest rate environment, which has stabilized following the tightening cycle of 2022-2023, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield trading at approximately 4.40% as of the effective date.

**Stabilized Net Operating Income:** \$4,876,800 per annum (as detailed in Section 7 below).

**As-Stabilized Value Calculation:**

\$4,876,800 ÷ 0.0640 = **\$76,200,000**

**Cross-Check:** The indicated as-stabilized value of \$76,200,000 implies a price per residential unit of approximately \$359,434 (\$76,200,000 ÷ 212 units). This metric falls within the range of \$340,000 to \$380,000 per unit observed for Class A new-construction multifamily properties in the downtown Durham submarket, confirming the reasonableness of the valuation conclusion. On a gross building area basis, the indicated value equates to approximately \$265.04 per square foot (\$76,200,000 ÷ 287,500 square feet), which is consistent with comparable market data.

**[Section 8 --- Environmental Considerations]{.underline}**

The appraiser reviewed the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\") prepared by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC, dated October 28, 2024. The Phase I ESA was prepared by the firm\'s lead environmental consultant, Dr. James Whitfield, P.E., in general conformance with ASTM Standard Practice E 1527-21 for Environmental Site Assessments. The Phase I ESA encompassed both parcels comprising the subject property.

The Phase I ESA identified one Recognized Environmental Condition (\"REC\") affecting the subject property: residual petroleum contamination associated with a former underground storage tank (\"UST\") located on the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 (615 Foster Street). Historical records indicate that the UST was originally installed in the 1950s in connection with the former tobacco warehouse operations and was used for the storage of heating oil. The UST had not been in active use since approximately 1988.

A Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase II ESA\") was subsequently conducted in August 2024, also by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC. The Phase II ESA included the advancement of soil borings and the collection and laboratory analysis of soil and groundwater samples from the area surrounding the former UST location. The results of the Phase II ESA revealed petroleum hydrocarbon contamination levels in soil that exceeded the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (\"NCDEQ\") Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch (\"IHSB\") residential soil screening levels for certain constituents, including benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (\"BTEX\"). However, the detected concentrations were below the applicable NCDEQ non-residential (commercial/industrial) soil screening levels.

Environmental remediation of the affected area was completed in September 2024. Remediation activities included the removal and proper disposal of the former UST, excavation and off-site disposal of approximately 320 cubic yards of petroleum-impacted soil, and post-remediation confirmation sampling. The remediation was performed under the oversight of NCDEQ and in accordance with an approved remediation work plan.

Following completion of the remediation, NCDEQ issued a No Further Action (\"NFA\") letter dated September 30, 2024, for the affected area. The NFA letter confirms that no further investigation or remediation is required, subject to the following conditions:

> \(i\) A soil vapor mitigation system must be installed and maintained in the structured parking garage and any enclosed occupied space constructed above the affected area, in accordance with specifications approved by NCDEQ; and
>
> \(ii\) Future use of the affected portion of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 --- specifically, an area encompassing approximately 0.38 acres in the northeast corner of the parcel --- is restricted to non-residential purposes. This land use restriction is memorialized in a Declaration of Land Use Restrictions recorded at the Durham County Register of Deeds.

The appraiser notes that the soil vapor mitigation system required by the NFA letter has been incorporated into the construction plans and specifications prepared by Meridian Design Collective PC and is included within the GMP contract with Graystone Construction Group Inc. The cost of the vapor mitigation system is reflected in the hard construction cost budget.

The NFA letter restricts future use of the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 (approximately 0.38 acres) to non-residential use. The appraiser notes this restriction for the record. The project plans, as reviewed by the appraiser and as described by the developer, include residential units on the upper floors of the building positioned above this area of the site. The appraiser\'s valuation assumes that the borrower will comply with all applicable environmental laws, regulations, and use restrictions, and that any required modifications, variances, or additional remediation necessary to permit the planned use will be obtained by the borrower at the borrower\'s cost. The appraiser expresses no opinion as to the legal permissibility of the planned residential use of the area above the environmentally restricted portion of the site. The appraiser has not adjusted the valuation conclusions to account for any potential impact of the NFA use restriction on the residential unit mix or leasability of units positioned above the restricted area.

The appraiser is not an environmental consultant and does not render opinions regarding environmental conditions, remediation adequacy, or compliance with environmental regulations. The reader is directed to the Phase I and Phase II ESA reports prepared by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC for a complete discussion of environmental matters.
