(b) **Exit Fee.** The Borrower shall pay the Lender, on the date of repayment in full of the Loan, an exit fee equal to (i) one-half of one percent (0.50%) of the outstanding principal balance if the Loan is repaid in full during the Construction Period, (ii) one-quarter of one percent (0.25%) of the outstanding principal balance if the Loan is repaid in full during the first six (6) months of the Mini-Perm Period, and (iii) zero if the Loan is repaid in full after the first six (6) months of the Mini-Perm Period. (c) **Unused Line Fee.** The Borrower shall pay the Lender a fee of one-quarter of one percent (0.25%) per annum on the average daily undrawn portion of the Commitment, payable quarterly in arrears, commencing with the first fiscal quarter ending after the Closing Date and continuing until the Commitment has been fully drawn or cancelled. (d) **Extension Fee.** Any Extension Fee shall be payable in accordance with Section 2.12. (e) **Fees Generally.** All fees are non-refundable when paid and, once paid, shall not be subject to reduction, setoff, or refund for any reason, including any prepayment or acceleration. Fees are in addition to, and not in lieu of, the Lender's expenses under Section 13.3.

**Section 2.11 — Prepayment.** The Loan may be prepaid in whole or in part at any time upon not less than five (5) Business Days' prior written notice to the Lender, subject to payment of accrued interest, the Exit Fee (if applicable), and any amounts owing under Section 13.3. No prepayment premium other than the Exit Fee applies. Amounts prepaid may not be reborrowed, and any partial prepayment shall not reduce the Commitment unless the Lender expressly agrees in writing. Partial prepayments shall be applied first to fees and costs, then to accrued interest, and then to principal, in inverse order of maturity.

**Section 2.12 — Extension Option.** (a) The Borrower may, at its option, extend the Mini-Perm Maturity Date by six (6) months to February 28, 2029 (the "Extended Maturity Date"), provided that each of the following conditions is satisfied as of the date of the Borrower's election and as of the Mini-Perm Maturity Date: (i) no Event of Default or Default exists and no event has occurred that, with notice or lapse of time or both, would constitute an Event of Default under any Loan Document or the Intercreditor Agreement; (ii) Substantial Completion has occurred and a final certificate of occupancy has been issued by the City of Durham for all residential units and retail bays; (iii) not less than seventy-five percent (75%) of the residential units are leased to tenants under executed leases of not less than twelve (12) months and are physically occupied; (iv) the DSCR, calculated using annualized in-place Net Operating Income for the most recent three (3)-month period divided by annual Interest Expense on the outstanding principal balance at the then-applicable Applicable Rate, is not less than 1.15x; (v) the Borrower has paid the Extension Fee; (vi) the Borrower has delivered evidence of an Interest Rate Cap Agreement for the Extension Period, with a strike rate and counterparty acceptable to the Lender (minimum long-term rating of A- from S&P or A3 from Moody's) and an aggregate notional amount not less than the outstanding principal balance; (vii) the Intercreditor Agreement remains in full force and effect and no default exists thereunder; (viii) the Lender has received an updated appraisal from an MAI-designated appraiser acceptable to the Lender confirming that the LTV based on the outstanding principal balance and the as-stabilized value does not exceed seventy percent (70%); (ix) all representations and warranties remain true and correct in all material respects; and (x) the Borrower has delivered written notice of its election to extend not less than sixty (60) days prior to the Mini-Perm Maturity Date. (b) The extension is not automatic, and time is of the essence. The Lender's acceptance of the Extension Fee shall not constitute a waiver of any unsatisfied condition. (c) The Extension Fee and the conditions in this Section 2.12 are Lender proposals not fixed by the executed Term Sheet; see Cover Memorandum Item M-20.

**Section 2.13 — Maturity; Commencement of Mini-Perm Period.** The outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall be due and payable in full on the Maturity Date. The Mini-Perm Period shall commence on the later of (a) the date of Substantial Completion and (b) the date on which the Construction Period would otherwise expire, and, in either case, only if no Event of Default then exists; provided, however, that the occurrence of the Mini-Perm Period shall not extend the Construction Maturity Date or the Mini-Perm Maturity Date.

**Section 2.14 — Increased Costs; Taxes; Illegality; Inability to Determine Rate.** (a) If any law, regulation, or directive (or any change in the interpretation thereof) after the Closing Date imposes on the Lender any cost or reserve requirement that increases the cost of making or maintaining the Loan, the Borrower shall pay the Lender such additional amounts as are necessary to compensate the Lender, upon presentation of a certificate detailing the calculation. (b) All payments shall be made free and clear of, and without deduction for, any taxes other than Excluded Taxes; if any deduction or withholding is required, the Borrower shall pay the amount necessary so that the Lender receives the amount it would have received absent the deduction, and shall furnish tax receipts. (c) If the Lender determines that (i) Daily Simple SOFR cannot be determined or is not available, (ii) any applicable law makes it unlawful for the Lender to make or maintain the Loan based on Daily Simple SOFR, or (iii) Daily Simple SOFR no longer adequately and fairly reflects the cost to the Lender of making or maintaining the Loan, then the Lender may suspend further Advances and shall implement a Benchmark Replacement in accordance with Section 2.15. (d) The Lender shall not be obligated to fund any Advance on any day on which Daily Simple SOFR is not published for the applicable Business Day.

**Section 2.15 — Benchmark Replacement.** (a) If the Lender determines that a public statement has been made by or on behalf of the administrator of SOFR or a regulatory supervisor announcing that SOFR is no longer representative or will no longer be provided, or that SOFR has otherwise become unavailable, the Lender may select a successor benchmark rate that is recommended or endorsed by the Alternative Reference Rates Committee ("ARRC") or, if no such rate is available, a rate selected by the Lender in its reasonable discretion. (b) Any Benchmark Replacement shall include (i) spread adjustments consistent with ARRC recommended best practices, (ii) a term or daily convention consistent with the replacement rate, (iii) notice to the Borrower as soon as practicable, and (iv) such conforming changes to the Loan Documents as the Lender reasonably determines are necessary. (c) The Lender shall not be liable for any determination made in good faith under this Section 2.15, and any such determination shall be binding on the Borrower absent manifest error.

**Section 1.2 — Interpretation.** (a) The words "include," "includes," and "including" are deemed to be followed by "without limitation." (b) "Hereof," "herein," "hereunder," and similar terms refer to this Agreement as a whole. (c) References to Articles, Sections, and Exhibits are to Articles and Sections of, and Exhibits to, this Agreement. (d) The singular includes the plural and vice versa; any gender includes all genders. (e) References to any statute, regulation, or agreement include amendments, successors, and replacements. (f) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. (g) "Writing," "written," and comparable terms refer to a writing that is printed, typewritten, or electronically transmitted and retrievable in perceivable form. (h) If any period expires on a day that is not a Business Day, the period expires on the next Business Day. (i) This Agreement has been negotiated by the parties with the assistance of counsel, and no rule of construction resolving ambiguities against the drafting party applies. (j) Any reference to the Lender's "satisfaction," "approval," "consent," or "determination" means such satisfaction, approval, consent, or determination in the Lender's reasonable judgment unless this Agreement expressly provides for sole or absolute discretion, in which case the Lender's sole and absolute discretion applies. (k) References to any amount "funded from Loan proceeds" mean that such amount is included in the Approved Budget and advanced under Article IV.

**Section 1.3 — Accounting Terms and Determinations.** All accounting terms not defined in this Agreement have the meanings given to them under GAAP. All financial statements, certificates, and compliance calculations required under this Agreement shall be prepared in accordance with GAAP consistently applied, except that the Borrower's net worth shall be determined on a consolidated basis for the Borrower only (excluding the assets or liabilities of any member), and shall include as an asset the Borrower's interest in the Property valued at the lower of cost or the most recent Appraised Value.

**Section 1.4 — Interest Conventions.** All determinations of Daily Simple SOFR, the Applicable Rate, the Default Rate, and interest payable under this Agreement shall be made by the Lender. The Lender shall not be required to notify the Borrower of any change in the Applicable Rate resulting from a change in Daily Simple SOFR, although the Lender shall provide the Borrower with monthly invoice statements reflecting the rate applied. Each determination by the Lender is conclusive absent manifest error.

## ARTICLE II — THE LOAN

**Section 2.1 — The Commitment; the Loan.** Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Lender agrees to make the Loan to the Borrower in one or more Advances on and after the Closing Date, in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed the Commitment. The Loan is a multiple-advance facility. Amounts repaid or prepaid may not be reborrowed. The Borrower's obligation to repay the Loan is evidenced by the Note.

**Section 2.2 — Purpose.** The proceeds of the Loan shall be used solely to (a) fund the hard and soft costs of the Project in accordance with the Approved Budget and the Approved Draw Schedule, (b) fund the Interest Reserve, (c) pay the Origination Fee to the extent permitted by Section 2.10, and (d) pay such other Project costs as are expressly approved by the Lender in writing. No portion of the Loan proceeds may be used to pay any distribution to any member of the Borrower, to repay any Indebtedness of any member or Affiliate of the Borrower, or to reimburse any member for any capital contribution, except as expressly approved in writing by the Lender.

**Section 2.3 — The Note.** The Loan shall be evidenced by the Note, which shall be payable to the order of the Lender in the principal amount of the Commitment and shall bear interest as provided in this Agreement and the Note. In the event of any conflict between the Note and this Agreement as to the payment of interest or principal, this Agreement controls.

**Section 2.4 — Condition of the Property; Lender Not a Builder.** The Lender is not a party to the Construction Contract or the architect's agreement and has no obligation to supervise, inspect, or inform the Borrower of any aspect of the Work. Any inspection or review performed by the Lender or the Construction Consultant is for the sole benefit of the Lender and does not constitute a warranty or representation as to the adequacy, sufficiency, quality, or compliance of the Work, the Approved Plans and Specifications, or the Approved Budget, nor does it relieve the Borrower or the General Contractor of any obligation.

**Section 2.5 — Interest Rate.** (a) During the Construction Period, the outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall bear interest at the Applicable Rate for the Construction Period. (b) During the Mini-Perm Period (including any Extension Period), the outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall bear interest at the Applicable Rate for the Mini-Perm Period. (c) Interest shall be computed on the basis of actual days elapsed over a three hundred sixty (360)-day year, applied to the actual outstanding principal balance each day, in accordance with Section 2.8. (d) The Alternate Basis for determining interest — *inapplicable; the Loan bears interest on a Daily Simple SOFR basis from the Closing Date.*

**Section 2.6 — SOFR Floor; Negative SOFR.** Daily Simple SOFR shall at no time be less than the SOFR Floor of 1.00% per annum. If Daily Simple SOFR would otherwise be negative, Daily Simple SOFR shall be deemed to be the SOFR Floor. The SOFR Floor applies during both the Construction Period and the Mini-Perm Period and may not be adjusted except through a Benchmark Replacement.

**Section 2.7 — Default Rate.** Upon and during the continuance of an Event of Default, and at the Lender's election from the date of the Event of Default (and, with respect to any Event of Default under Section 11.5, automatically and without notice), all outstanding amounts under the Loan Documents shall bear interest at the Default Rate, being the Applicable Rate plus five percent (5.00%) per annum, and interest at the Default Rate shall be payable on demand and shall be secured by the Loan Documents.

**Section 2.8 — Computation of Interest; Usury Savings.** (a) Interest for each day shall equal the product of (i) the outstanding principal balance on that day, (ii) the Applicable Rate in effect for that day divided by three hundred sixty (360), and (iii) the number of days elapsed. (b) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any Loan Document, no provision of any Loan Document shall require the payment or permit the collection of interest in excess of the maximum rate permitted by applicable North Carolina law (the "Maximum Lawful Rate"). If any excess interest is provided for or received, (i) the excess shall be applied first to unpaid principal, then to other Obligations, and then refunded to the Borrower, and (ii) the effective rate of interest shall be automatically reduced to the Maximum Lawful Rate. To the extent permitted by applicable law, all interest at any time contracted for, charged, or received shall be amortized, prorated, allocated, and spread over the full period of the Loan.

**Section 2.9 — Payments.** (a) Accrued interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall be payable monthly in arrears on the first Business Day of each calendar month, commencing on the first Business Day of the first full calendar month following the Closing Date. (b) During the Construction Period, interest shall be paid from the Interest Reserve Account until the Interest Reserve is exhausted; thereafter, and during the Mini-Perm Period, interest shall be payable by the Borrower from its own funds (subject to Section 4.8 and the Carry Guaranty). (c) The outstanding principal balance of the Loan, together with all accrued and unpaid interest, fees, costs, and other Obligations, shall be due and payable in full on the Maturity Date. (d) All payments shall be made in immediately available funds to the account designated by the Lender, without setoff, counterclaim, deduction, or withholding, not later than 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on the due date. (e) If any payment is not received within five (5) days after its due date, the Borrower shall pay a late charge equal to five percent (5.00%) of the overdue amount, in addition to interest at the Default Rate; such late charge shall not constitute a substitute for the Lender's other remedies and shall not cure any Event of Default.

**Section 2.10 — Fees.** (a) **Origination Fee.** The Borrower shall pay the Lender an origination fee of Four Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($475,000), being one percent (1.00%) of the Commitment. The Origination Fee is fully earned on the Closing Date, is non-refundable, and may be funded from the Loan proceeds as reflected in the Approved Budget and Exhibit D. (b) **Exit Fee.** The Borrower shall pay the Lender, on the date of repayment in full of the Loan, an exit fee equal to (i) one-half of one percent (0.50%) of the outstanding principal balance if the Loan is repaid in full during the Construction Period, (ii) one-quarter of one percent (0.25%) of the outstanding principal balance if the Loan is repaid in full during the first six (6) months of the Mini-Perm Period, and (iii) zero if the Loan is repaid in full after the first six (6) months of the Mini-Perm Period. (c) **Unused Line Fee.** The Borrower shall pay the Lender a fee of one-quarter of one percent (0.25%) per annum on the average daily undrawn portion of the Commitment, payable quarterly in arrears, commencing with the first fiscal quarter ending after the Closing Date and continuing until the Commitment has been fully drawn or cancelled. (d) **Extension Fee.** Any Extension Fee shall be payable in accordance with Section 2.12. (e) **Fees Generally.** All fees are non-refundable when paid and, once paid, shall not be subject to reduction, setoff, or refund for any reason, including any prepayment or acceleration. Fees are in addition to, and not in lieu of, the Lender's expenses under Section 13.3.

**Section 2.11 — Prepayment.** The Loan may be prepaid in whole or in part at any time upon not less than five (5) Business Days' prior written notice to the Lender, subject to payment of accrued interest, the Exit Fee (if applicable), and any amounts owing under Section 13.3. No prepayment premium other than the Exit Fee applies. Amounts prepaid may not be reborrowed, and any partial prepayment shall not reduce the Commitment unless the Lender expressly agrees in writing. Partial prepayments shall be applied first to fees and costs, then to accrued interest, and then to principal, in inverse order of maturity.

**Section 2.12 — Extension Option.** (a) The Borrower may, at its option, extend the Mini-Perm Maturity Date by six (6) months to February 28, 2029 (the "Extended Maturity Date"), provided that each of the following conditions is satisfied as of the date of the Borrower's election and as of the Mini-Perm Maturity Date: (i) no Event of Default or Default exists and no event has occurred that, with notice or lapse of time or both, would constitute an Event of Default under any Loan Document or the Intercreditor Agreement; (ii) Substantial Completion has occurred and a final certificate of occupancy has been issued by the City of Durham for all residential units and retail bays; (iii) not less than seventy-five percent (75%) of the residential units are leased to tenants under executed leases of not less than twelve (12) months and are physically occupied; (iv) the DSCR, calculated using annualized in-place Net Operating Income for the most recent three (3)-month period divided by annual Interest Expense on the outstanding principal balance at the then-applicable Applicable Rate, is not less than 1.15x; (v) the Borrower has paid the Extension Fee; (vi) the Borrower has delivered evidence of an Interest Rate Cap Agreement for the Extension Period, with a strike rate and counterparty acceptable to the Lender (minimum long-term rating of A- from S&P or A3 from Moody's) and an aggregate notional amount not less than the outstanding principal balance; (vii) the Intercreditor Agreement remains in full force and effect and no default exists thereunder; (viii) the Lender has received an updated appraisal from an MAI-designated appraiser acceptable to the Lender confirming that the LTV based on the outstanding principal balance and the as-stabilized value does not exceed seventy percent (70%); (ix) all representations and warranties remain true and correct in all material respects; and (x) the Borrower has delivered written notice of its election to extend not less than sixty (60) days prior to the Mini-Perm Maturity Date. (b) The extension is not automatic, and time is of the essence. The Lender's acceptance of the Extension Fee shall not constitute a waiver of any unsatisfied condition. (c) The Extension Fee and the conditions in this Section 2.12 are Lender proposals not fixed by the executed Term Sheet; see Cover Memorandum Item M-20.

**Section 2.13 — Maturity; Commencement of Mini-Perm Period.** The outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall be due and payable in full on the Maturity Date. The Mini-Perm Period shall commence on the later of (a) the date of Substantial Completion and (b) the date on which the Construction Period would otherwise expire, and, in either case, only if no Event of Default then exists; provided, however, that the occurrence of the Mini-Perm Period shall not extend the Construction Maturity Date or the Mini-Perm Maturity Date.

**Section 2.14 — Increased Costs; Taxes; Illegality; Inability to Determine Rate.** (a) If any law, regulation, or directive (or any change in the interpretation thereof) after the Closing Date imposes on the Lender any cost or reserve requirement that increases the cost of making or maintaining the Loan, the Borrower shall pay the Lender such additional amounts as are necessary to compensate the Lender, upon presentation of a certificate detailing the calculation. (b) All payments shall be made free and clear of, and without deduction for, any taxes other than Excluded Taxes; if any deduction or withholding is required, the Borrower shall pay the amount necessary so that the Lender receives the amount it would have received absent the deduction, and shall furnish tax receipts. (c) If the Lender determines that (i) Daily Simple SOFR cannot be determined or is not available, (ii) any applicable law makes it unlawful for the Lender to make or maintain the Loan based on Daily Simple SOFR, or (iii) Daily Simple SOFR no longer adequately and fairly reflects the cost to the Lender of making or maintaining the Loan, then the Lender may suspend further Advances and shall implement a Benchmark Replacement in accordance with Section 2.15. (d) The Lender shall not be obligated to fund any Advance on any day on which Daily Simple SOFR is not published for the applicable Business Day.

**Section 2.15 — Benchmark Replacement.** (a) If the Lender determines that a public statement has been made by or on behalf of the administrator of SOFR or a regulatory supervisor announcing that SOFR is no longer representative or will no longer be provided, or that SOFR has otherwise become unavailable, the Lender may select a successor benchmark rate that is recommended or endorsed by the Alternative Reference Rates Committee ("ARRC") or, if no such rate is available, a rate selected by the Lender in its reasonable discretion. (b) Any Benchmark Replacement shall include (i) spread adjustments consistent with ARRC recommended best practices, (ii) a term or daily convention consistent with the replacement rate, (iii) notice to the Borrower as soon as practicable, and (iv) such conforming changes to the Loan Documents as the Lender reasonably determines are necessary. (c) The Lender shall not be liable for any determination made in good faith under this Section 2.15, and any such determination shall be binding on the Borrower absent manifest error.

EOF

## ARTICLE III — CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO CLOSING

The Lender's obligation to make the initial Advance is subject to the prior satisfaction (or written waiver by the Lender, in its sole discretion) of each of the following conditions, each in form and substance satisfactory to the Lender and its counsel:

**Section 3.1 — Loan Documents.** The Borrower and each Guarantor shall have executed and delivered each of the Loan Documents, including this Agreement, the Note, the Deed of Trust, the Assignment of Rents, the Security Agreement, the UCC-1 financing statements, the Collateral Assignments, the Pledge Agreements, the Pledge Account Control Agreements, the Cash Management Agreement, the Completion Guaranty, the Carry Guaranty, the Partial Repayment Guaranty, the Environmental Indemnity, and the Intercreditor Agreement.

**Section 3.2 — Organizational Documents; Authority.** The Lender shall have received (a) a certificate of good standing for the Borrower issued by the North Carolina Secretary of State not more than thirty (30) days prior to the Closing Date; (b) certified copies of the Borrower's articles of organization and Operating Agreement, as amended in accordance with Section 3.10; (c) a certificate of the Borrower's managing member attaching resolutions or written consents of all members authorizing the Loan, the execution and delivery of the Loan Documents, the granting of the security interests, the Pledge Agreements, and the transactions contemplated hereby; (d) customary certificates of incumbency and signature; and (e) evidence that each pledge of Membership Interests has been duly authorized by the Managing Member and by members holding not less than seventy-five percent (75%) of the Membership Interests as required by Section 9.1 of the Operating Agreement.

**Section 3.3 — Financial Statements and Certificates.** The Lender shall have received (a) the Borrower's audited or reviewed financial statements for its two most recent Fiscal Years and interim statements for the most recent fiscal quarter; (b) a certificate of the Managing Member certifying that the Borrower's net worth is not less than Twelve Million Dollars ($12,000,000); (c) current personal financial statements for each Guarantor dated not earlier than December 15, 2024, together with supporting documentation reasonably requested by the Lender; (d) federal income tax returns for the Borrower and each Guarantor for the two most recent taxable years; and (e) a certificate evidencing combined Guarantor liquidity of not less than Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000), with not less than One Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,500,000) attributable to each Guarantor individually.

**Section 3.4 — Title Insurance; Survey; Zoning.** The Lender shall have received (a) the Title Policy (or a binding and unconditional commitment to issue the Title Policy at the Closing, together with an insured closing letter from the Title Insurer), in an amount not less than the Commitment, insuring the Deed of Trust as a valid first-priority lien on the Property subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, and containing no exception for the Triangle Commercial Bank deed of trust recorded in Book 6215, Page 892, Durham County Registry, and no exception for mechanic's or materialmen's liens arising from work performed prior to the Closing Date; (b) a current ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey complying with the 2021 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements (including Table A items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, and 21 as specified by the Lender), certified to the Lender, the Title Insurer, and the Borrower, dated or re-certified within ninety (90) days of the Closing Date; (c) a zoning compliance letter from the City of Durham confirming that the Project is permitted as of right in the MU-D district; and (d) such endorsements as the Lender may require, including access, contiguity, survey, comprehensive, zoning 3.0, subdivision, location, usury, tie-in, and mechanic's lien coverage (or such other protection as the Lender may require, including an owner's affidavit, payment affidavits, and a title indemnity).

**Section 3.5 — Appraisal.** The Lender shall have received and reviewed the full self-contained appraisal report dated November 15, 2024 prepared by Ridgeline Appraisal Services Inc. (Linda M. Haverford, MAI; File No. RAS-2024-1147) concluding an as-is value of not less than $8,900,000, an as-completed value of not less than $72,800,000, and an as-stabilized value of not less than $76,200,000, which appraisal shall have been reviewed and approved by the Lender's appraisal review department in accordance with the requirements of Title XI of FIRREA and the applicable regulations of the OCC. The Lender may require an update of the appraisal or a new appraisal if the Closing Date occurs more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the date of value.

**Section 3.6 — Environmental.** The Lender shall have received, reviewed, and approved, each in form and substance satisfactory to the Lender: (a) the Phase I ESA, together with a reliance letter from Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC naming the Lender as an intended reliance party; (b) the Phase II ESA; (c) the NFA Letter; (d) evidence that the Land Use Restriction has been recorded in the Durham County Registry of Deeds in accordance with condition 4 of the NFA Letter, or such other evidence of compliance as the Lender may accept; (e) evidence that the Soil Management Plan has been prepared and submitted to NCDEQ and, if required, approved; (f) evidence that the soil vapor mitigation system required by condition 1 of the NFA Letter has been designed by a professional engineer licensed in North Carolina and is incorporated into the Approved Plans and Specifications and the Construction Contract; (g) resolution of the conflict between the non-residential use restriction applicable to the Restricted Area and the residential use proposed in the Project, in a manner described in Section 6.5(d); and (h) a Phase I update satisfying 40 C.F.R. § 312.20(c) if the Closing Date occurs after April 26, 2025.

**Section 3.7 — Construction Contract; Architect; Consultant.** The Lender shall have received (a) a true and complete copy of the fully executed Construction Contract, together with the General Contractor's consent to collateral assignment, evidence of the General Contractor's financial capacity and payment and performance bonding capacity (including a 100% performance and payment bond, or such other assurance as the Lender may require), and the General Contractor's schedule of values; (b) a true and complete copy of the fully executed architect's agreement with the Architect, together with the Architect's consent to collateral assignment and evidence of professional liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000; (c) the final Approved Plans and Specifications and all permits necessary to commence the Work; (d) the Approved Budget in line-item detail and the Approved Draw Schedule, each reconciled to this Agreement as contemplated by Section 8.1; and (e) the Construction Consultant's initial report confirming that the Approved Budget and the Approved Draw Schedule are sufficient to complete the Work and that the Project is feasible as designed.

**Section 3.8 — Insurance.** The Lender shall have received certificates of insurance and, where requested, certified copies of policies, evidencing each coverage required by Article VI and **Exhibit G**, naming the Lender as mortgagee, additional insured, and/or loss payee as its interests may appear, with such lender's loss payable and mortgagee endorsements as the Lender may require, and with not less than thirty (30) days' notice of cancellation (ten (10) days for non-payment of premium).

**Section 3.9 — Loan-to-Cost Compliance; Equity.** The Lender shall have received evidence that, immediately after giving effect to the initial Advance, the Loan-to-Cost Ratio does not exceed eighty percent (80.0%). Because the Loan-to-Cost Ratio computed on the Commitment of $47,500,000 and Total Project Costs of $56,700,000 equals 83.77%, this condition requires, on or before the Closing Date, either (a) a permanent reduction of the Commitment to Forty-Five Million Three Hundred Sixty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($45,360,000) (the "Reduced Commitment"), together with a conforming restatement of the Note, the Approved Budget, and **Exhibit D**, or (b) a written determination by the Lender, supported by documentation approved by the Lender, that Total Project Costs have increased to not less than Fifty-Nine Million Three Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($59,375,000), or (c) such combination of the foregoing as produces a Loan-to-Cost Ratio of not more than 80.0%. *A cash equity deposit alone does not satisfy this condition, because the Loan-to-Cost Ratio is a function of the principal amount of the Loan and Total Project Costs and is not reduced by the addition of a source of funds; see Cover Memorandum Item M-1.* If the Commitment is reduced under this Section, the Lender shall nonetheless have received evidence that the Borrower has deposited not less than Two Million One Hundred Forty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($2,140,000) into the Equity Escrow Account from sources other than the Mezzanine Loan, the Mezzanine Lender, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Thomas R. Chen, or any Affiliate of any of the foregoing, which deposit shall be disbursed under Section 4.9.

**Section 3.10 — Single-Purpose Entity; Operating Agreement Amendments; Non-Consolidation Opinion.** The Lender shall have received (a) evidence that the Operating Agreement has been amended to include the separateness covenants and the independent manager provisions required by Article XIV, and to revise Article III (Major Decisions) and Article IX (Transfer Restrictions) as required by Section 9.5(d) and Section 14.2; (b) a certificate of the Borrower confirming the appointment of an Independent Manager meeting the requirements of Section 14.2; and (c) the Non-Consolidation Opinion.

**Section 3.11 — Mezzanine Loan; Intercreditor Agreement.** The Lender shall have received (a) true and complete copies of the executed Mezzanine Documents, including the Mezzanine Lender's closing statement and full amortization schedule (including all payment-in-kind accruals); (b) the executed Intercreditor Agreement, which shall be in full force and effect and which shall provide, among other things, for the subordination of the Mezzanine Lender's pledge of the Membership Interests to the Lender's first-priority security interest, a standstill period of not less than ninety (90) days, cure rights and a purchase option in favor of the Mezzanine Lender, restrictions on amendments to the Mezzanine Documents without the Lender's consent, and bankruptcy-related restrictions; (c) evidence that the Mezzanine Lender has executed and delivered UCC-3 amendments subordinating any UCC-1 financing statement filed by it against the Borrower, and (d) UCC, tax lien, judgment, litigation, and bankruptcy searches confirming the Lender's first-priority position, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions.

**Section 3.12 — Release of Prior Encumbrance.** The Lender shall have received (a) a payoff letter from Triangle Commercial Bank (or its successor or assign) dated not more than thirty (30) days prior to the Closing Date, stating the outstanding principal balance, accrued interest, per diem, and all fees and charges required to obtain a full release of the deed of trust recorded in Book 6215, Page 892, Durham County Registry; (b) a recorded cancellation or certificate of satisfaction in recordable form executed in accordance with N.C.G.S. § 45-37, or a release to be recorded simultaneously with the Deed of Trust under an escrow arrangement satisfactory to the Title Insurer; (c) evidence that no guaranty, indemnity, or other obligation of the Borrower or any member survives the payoff and release; and (d) evidence that the payoff amount has been deposited with the Title Insurer for disbursement at the Closing from sources identified in Section 3.9 or otherwise approved by the Lender. *The Approved Budget and the Sources and Uses of Funds contain no line item for this payoff; see Cover Memorandum Item M-5.*

**Section 3.13 — Budget Detail; No Unfunded Items.** The Lender shall have received a line-item budget reconciled to the Sources and Uses of Funds on **Exhibit C**, together with the Borrower's certification that (a) the Approved Budget includes all costs necessary to complete the Work and to satisfy the conditions of the NFA Letter, (b) no cost of the Project is unfunded, and (c) the sources of funds are sufficient, together with the Loan proceeds, to complete the Project. The Lender shall have received evidence reasonably satisfactory to it of the sources of the Borrower's equity, including a tracing of the funds used to acquire the Property.

**Section 3.14 — Legal Opinions.** The Lender shall have received opinions of Borrower's counsel (Calloway & Strauss PLLC) addressed to the Lender as to due organization, valid existence, due authorization, execution and delivery, enforceability of the Loan Documents, perfection and first priority of the Lender's security interests (including the pledge of Membership Interests and the enforceability of the Lender's remedies against the Membership Interests notwithstanding the transfer restrictions in Section 9.1 of the Operating Agreement), the non-consolidation opinion, and such other matters as the Lender may reasonably require.

**Section 3.15 — CC&R and Architectural Review Approval.** The Lender shall have received evidence that the Association's Architectural Review Committee has approved the Approved Plans and Specifications in accordance with Article V of the Declaration recorded in Book 6984, Page 1155, Durham County Registry (as amended in Book 7102, Page 388), or that the sixty (60)-day deemed-approval period has expired without written action by the Architectural Review Committee, and such estoppel, consent to the Deed of Trust, or subordination as the Lender may reasonably require.

**Section 3.16 — Governmental Approvals.** The Lender shall have received evidence that all building permits, grading permits, utility approvals, and other governmental approvals necessary to commence and complete the Work have been obtained or will be obtained prior to the commencement of the applicable phase of the Work, together with copies of all permits issued.

**Section 3.17 — Fees and Expenses.** The Borrower shall have paid the Origination Fee (to the extent not funded under Section 2.10(a)), all fees of the Lender's counsel, the Title Insurer's premiums and charges, the Construction Consultant's fees, and all other costs and expenses required to be paid by the Borrower at Closing under Section 13.3.

**Section 3.18 — No Default; No Material Adverse Change.** No Event of Default or Default shall exist, and no Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred, including any material adverse change in the financial condition of the Borrower or either Guarantor, in general real estate market conditions, or in the availability of construction financing or permanent take-out financing for projects of the type of the Project.

**Section 3.19 — Flood Determination.** The Lender shall have received a current Standard Flood Hazard Determination confirming whether any portion of the Property is located in a Special Flood Hazard Area, and, if so, evidence of flood insurance in the amount required by the National Flood Insurance Act and the Lender's flood insurance policy.

**Section 3.20 — Additional Conditions.** The Lender shall have received such other documents, instruments, certificates, consents, and opinions as the Lender or its counsel may reasonably require, including (a) consents of all members of the Borrower to the Pledge Agreements and the Intercreditor Agreement, (b) the General Contractor's and Architect's consents to collateral assignment, (c) confirmation that no labor or materials have been furnished to the Property other than as disclosed in the Title Policy, together with lien waivers and paid receipts from the demolition contractor and the environmental remediation contractor, and (d) evidence of compliance with the USA PATRIOT Act and the Lender's customer due diligence requirements.

**Section 3.3 — Financial Statements and Certificates.** The Lender shall have received (a) the Borrower's audited or reviewed financial statements for its two most recent Fiscal Years and interim statements for the most recent fiscal quarter; (b) a certificate of the Managing Member certifying that the Borrower's net worth is not less than Twelve Million Dollars ($12,000,000); (c) current personal financial statements for each Guarantor dated not earlier than December 15, 2024, together with supporting documentation reasonably requested by the Lender; (d) federal income tax returns for the Borrower and each Guarantor for the two most recent taxable years; and (e) a certificate evidencing combined Guarantor liquidity of not less than Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000), with not less than One Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,500,000) attributable to each Guarantor individually.

**Section 3.4 — Title Insurance; Survey; Zoning.** The Lender shall have received (a) the Title Policy (or a binding and unconditional commitment to issue the Title Policy at the Closing, together with an insured closing letter from the Title Insurer), in an amount not less than the Commitment, insuring the Deed of Trust as a valid first-priority lien on the Property subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, and containing no exception for the Triangle Commercial Bank deed of trust recorded in Book 6215, Page 892, Durham County Registry, and no exception for mechanic's or materialmen's liens arising from work performed prior to the Closing Date; (b) a current ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey complying with the 2021 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements (including Table A items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, and 21 as specified by the Lender), certified to the Lender, the Title Insurer, and the Borrower, dated or re-certified within ninety (90) days of the Closing Date; (c) a zoning compliance letter from the City of Durham confirming that the Project is permitted as of right in the MU-D district; and (d) such endorsements as the Lender may require, including access, contiguity, survey, comprehensive, zoning 3.0, subdivision, location, usury, tie-in, and mechanic's lien coverage (or such other protection as the Lender may require, including an owner's affidavit, payment affidavits, and a title indemnity).

**Section 3.5 — Appraisal.** The Lender shall have received and reviewed the full self-contained appraisal report dated November 15, 2024 prepared by Ridgeline Appraisal Services Inc. (Linda M. Haverford, MAI; File No. RAS-2024-1147) concluding an as-is value of not less than $8,900,000, an as-completed value of not less than $72,800,000, and an as-stabilized value of not less than $76,200,000, which appraisal shall have been reviewed and approved by the Lender's appraisal review department in accordance with the requirements of Title XI of FIRREA and the applicable regulations of the OCC. The Lender may require an update of the appraisal or a new appraisal if the Closing Date occurs more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the date of value.

**Section 3.6 — Environmental.** The Lender shall have received, reviewed, and approved, each in form and substance satisfactory to the Lender: (a) the Phase I ESA, together with a reliance letter from Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC naming the Lender as an intended reliance party; (b) the Phase II ESA; (c) the NFA Letter; (d) evidence that the Land Use Restriction has been recorded in the Durham County Registry of Deeds in accordance with condition 4 of the NFA Letter, or such other evidence of compliance as the Lender may accept; (e) evidence that the Soil Management Plan has been prepared and submitted to NCDEQ and, if required, approved; (f) evidence that the soil vapor mitigation system required by condition 1 of the NFA Letter has been designed by a professional engineer licensed in North Carolina and is incorporated into the Approved Plans and Specifications and the Construction Contract; (g) resolution of the conflict between the non-residential use restriction applicable to the Restricted Area and the residential use proposed in the Project, in a manner described in Section 6.5(d); and (h) a Phase I update satisfying 40 C.F.R. § 312.20(c) if the Closing Date occurs after April 26, 2025.

**Section 3.7 — Construction Contract; Architect; Consultant.** The Lender shall have received (a) a true and complete copy of the fully executed Construction Contract, together with the General Contractor's consent to collateral assignment, evidence of the General Contractor's financial capacity and payment and performance bonding capacity (including a 100% performance and payment bond, or such other assurance as the Lender may require), and the General Contractor's schedule of values; (b) a true and complete copy of the fully executed architect's agreement with the Architect, together with the Architect's consent to collateral assignment and evidence of professional liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000; (c) the final Approved Plans and Specifications and all permits necessary to commence the Work; (d) the Approved Budget in line-item detail and the Approved Draw Schedule, each reconciled to this Agreement as contemplated by Section 8.1; and (e) the Construction Consultant's initial report confirming that the Approved Budget and the Approved Draw Schedule are sufficient to complete the Work and that the Project is feasible as designed.

**Section 3.8 — Insurance.** The Lender shall have received certificates of insurance and, where requested, certified copies of policies, evidencing each coverage required by Article VI and **Exhibit G**, naming the Lender as mortgagee, additional insured, and/or loss payee as its interests may appear, with such lender's loss payable and mortgagee endorsements as the Lender may require, and with not less than thirty (30) days' notice of cancellation (ten (10) days for non-payment of premium).

**Section 3.9 — Loan-to-Cost Compliance; Equity.** The Lender shall have received evidence that, immediately after giving effect to the initial Advance, the Loan-to-Cost Ratio does not exceed eighty percent (80.0%). Because the Loan-to-Cost Ratio computed on the Commitment of $47,500,000 and Total Project Costs of $56,700,000 equals 83.77%, this condition requires, on or before the Closing Date, either (a) a permanent reduction of the Commitment to Forty-Five Million Three Hundred Sixty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($45,360,000) (the "Reduced Commitment"), together with a conforming restatement of the Note, the Approved Budget, and **Exhibit D**, or (b) a written determination by the Lender, supported by documentation approved by the Lender, that Total Project Costs have increased to not less than Fifty-Nine Million Three Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($59,375,000), or (c) such combination of the foregoing as produces a Loan-to-Cost Ratio of not more than 80.0%. *A cash equity deposit alone does not satisfy this condition, because the Loan-to-Cost Ratio is a function of the principal amount of the Loan and Total Project Costs and is not reduced by the addition of a source of funds; see Cover Memorandum Item M-1.* If the Commitment is reduced under this Section, the Lender shall nonetheless have received evidence that the Borrower has deposited not less than Two Million One Hundred Forty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($2,140,000) into the Equity Escrow Account from sources other than the Mezzanine Loan, the Mezzanine Lender, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Thomas R. Chen, or any Affiliate of any of the foregoing, which deposit shall be disbursed under Section 4.9.

**Section 3.10 — Single-Purpose Entity; Operating Agreement Amendments; Non-Consolidation Opinion.** The Lender shall have received (a) evidence that the Operating Agreement has been amended to include the separateness covenants and the independent manager provisions required by Article XIV, and to revise Article III (Major Decisions) and Article IX (Transfer Restrictions) as required by Section 9.5(d) and Section 14.2; (b) a certificate of the Borrower confirming the appointment of an Independent Manager meeting the requirements of Section 14.2; and (c) the Non-Consolidation Opinion.

**Section 3.11 — Mezzanine Loan; Intercreditor Agreement.** The Lender shall have received (a) true and complete copies of the executed Mezzanine Documents, including the Mezzanine Lender's closing statement and full amortization schedule (including all payment-in-kind accruals); (b) the executed Intercreditor Agreement, which shall be in full force and effect and which shall provide, among other things, for the subordination of the Mezzanine Lender's pledge of the Membership Interests to the Lender's first-priority security interest, a standstill period of not less than ninety (90) days, cure rights and a purchase option in favor of the Mezzanine Lender, restrictions on amendments to the Mezzanine Documents without the Lender's consent, and bankruptcy-related restrictions; (c) evidence that the Mezzanine Lender has executed and delivered UCC-3 amendments subordinating any UCC-1 financing statement filed by it against the Borrower, and (d) UCC, tax lien, judgment, litigation, and bankruptcy searches confirming the Lender's first-priority position, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions.

**Section 3.12 — Release of Prior Encumbrance.** The Lender shall have received (a) a payoff letter from Triangle Commercial Bank (or its successor or assign) dated not more than thirty (30) days prior to the Closing Date, stating the outstanding principal balance, accrued interest, per diem, and all fees and charges required to obtain a full release of the deed of trust recorded in Book 6215, Page 892, Durham County Registry; (b) a recorded cancellation or certificate of satisfaction in recordable form executed in accordance with N.C.G.S. § 45-37, or a release to be recorded simultaneously with the Deed of Trust under an escrow arrangement satisfactory to the Title Insurer; (c) evidence that no guaranty, indemnity, or other obligation of the Borrower or any member survives the payoff and release; and (d) evidence that the payoff amount has been deposited with the Title Insurer for disbursement at the Closing from sources identified in Section 3.9 or otherwise approved by the Lender. *The Approved Budget and the Sources and Uses of Funds contain no line item for this payoff; see Cover Memorandum Item M-5.*

**Section 3.13 — Budget Detail; No Unfunded Items.** The Lender shall have received a line-item budget reconciled to the Sources and Uses of Funds on **Exhibit C**, together with the Borrower's certification that (a) the Approved Budget includes all costs necessary to complete the Work and to satisfy the conditions of the NFA Letter, (b) no cost of the Project is unfunded, and (c) the sources of funds are sufficient, together with the Loan proceeds, to complete the Project. The Lender shall have received evidence reasonably satisfactory to it of the sources of the Borrower's equity, including a tracing of the funds used to acquire the Property.

**Section 3.14 — Legal Opinions.** The Lender shall have received opinions of Borrower's counsel (Calloway & Strauss PLLC) addressed to the Lender as to due organization, valid existence, due authorization, execution and delivery, enforceability of the Loan Documents, perfection and first priority of the Lender's security interests (including the pledge of Membership Interests and the enforceability of the Lender's remedies against the Membership Interests notwithstanding the transfer restrictions in Section 9.1 of the Operating Agreement), the non-consolidation opinion, and such other matters as the Lender may reasonably require.

**Section 3.15 — CC&R and Architectural Review Approval.** The Lender shall have received evidence that the Association's Architectural Review Committee has approved the Approved Plans and Specifications in accordance with Article V of the Declaration recorded in Book 6984, Page 1155, Durham County Registry (as amended in Book 7102, Page 388), or that the sixty (60)-day deemed-approval period has expired without written action by the Architectural Review Committee, and such estoppel, consent to the Deed of Trust, or subordination as the Lender may reasonably require.

**Section 3.16 — Governmental Approvals.** The Lender shall have received evidence that all building permits, grading permits, utility approvals, and other governmental approvals necessary to commence and complete the Work have been obtained or will be obtained prior to the commencement of the applicable phase of the Work, together with copies of all permits issued.

**Section 3.17 — Fees and Expenses.** The Borrower shall have paid the Origination Fee (to the extent not funded under Section 2.10(a)), all fees of the Lender's counsel, the Title Insurer's premiums and charges, the Construction Consultant's fees, and all other costs and expenses required to be paid by the Borrower at Closing under Section 13.3.

**Section 3.18 — No Default; No Material Adverse Change.** No Event of Default or Default shall exist, and no Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred, including any material adverse change in the financial condition of the Borrower or either Guarantor, in general real estate market conditions, or in the availability of construction financing or permanent take-out financing for projects of the type of the Project.

**Section 3.19 — Flood Determination.** The Lender shall have received a current Standard Flood Hazard Determination confirming whether any portion of the Property is located in a Special Flood Hazard Area, and, if so, evidence of flood insurance in the amount required by the National Flood Insurance Act and the Lender's flood insurance policy.

**Section 3.20 — Additional Conditions.** The Lender shall have received such other documents, instruments, certificates, consents, and opinions as the Lender or its counsel may reasonably require, including (a) consents of all members of the Borrower to the Pledge Agreements and the Intercreditor Agreement, (b) the General Contractor's and Architect's consents to collateral assignment, (c) confirmation that no labor or materials have been furnished to the Property other than as disclosed in the Title Policy, together with lien waivers and paid receipts from the demolition contractor and the environmental remediation contractor, and (d) evidence of compliance with the USA PATRIOT Act and the Lender's customer due diligence requirements.

## ARTICLE IV — ADVANCES, DISBURSEMENT AND RETAINAGE

**Section 4.1 — Draw Requests.** The Borrower may request an Advance not more frequently than once per calendar month by delivering a Draw Request to the Lender not less than fifteen (15) days prior to the requested funding date. Each Draw Request shall (a) specify the requested Advance amount, (b) identify the milestone or budget line items being funded and the percentage of completion of each, (c) be accompanied by the documentation required by Section 4.2, and (d) be certified by a Responsible Officer as true, correct, and complete. The Lender shall use commercially reasonable efforts to process a complete Draw Request within ten (10) Business Days after receipt; the Lender's failure to process a Draw Request within that period shall not constitute a waiver of any condition or a default by the Lender.

**Section 4.2 — Supporting Documentation.** Each Draw Request shall be accompanied by: (a) an AIA Application and Certificate for Payment (Form G702) and Continuation Sheet (Form G703) certified by the Architect and the General Contractor; (b) the Construction Consultant's report confirming achievement of the milestone and the percentage of completion; (c) an updated construction progress report and schedule prepared by the Borrower and the General Contractor, together with a change order log; (d) partial lien waivers in statutory form under N.C.G.S. Chapter 44A from the General Contractor, each subcontractor, and each materialman, for all work performed and materials supplied through the end of the prior draw period; (e) a date-down title endorsement from the Title Insurer confirming no intervening liens, encumbrances, or title defects since the prior endorsement (and, for the initial Advance, since the effective date of the Title Policy); (f) evidence that all insurance required by Article VI remains in full force and effect; (g) an updated budget reconciliation demonstrating that the remaining Loan proceeds, equity, and Contingency Reserve are sufficient to complete the Work; (h) a certification that no Default or Event of Default exists and that all representations and warranties remain true and correct in all material respects; and (i) such other documentation as the Lender may reasonably require.

**Section 4.3 — Inspections.** The Lender may, at the Borrower's expense, cause the Construction Consultant to inspect the Property and the Work prior to each Advance and at such other times as the Lender may reasonably determine, and the Borrower shall make the Property and all construction records available for inspection during normal business hours upon reasonable notice. The Lender may also inspect the Property itself at any time during normal business hours upon reasonable notice.

**Section 4.4 — Conditions Precedent to Each Advance.** The Lender's obligation to make any Advance (including the initial Advance) is subject to satisfaction of each of the following as of the funding date: (a) all conditions in Article III remain satisfied; (b) no Default or Event of Default exists and no event has occurred that with notice or lapse of time or both would constitute an Event of Default; (c) all representations and warranties remain true and correct in all material respects; (d) the Borrower has delivered a complete Draw Request and the documentation required by Section 4.2; (e) the Construction Consultant has confirmed the milestone and that sufficient funds remain to complete the Work; (f) the Loan-to-Cost Ratio, the Loan-to-Value Ratios, the DSCR, and each other financial covenant in Article VIII are satisfied on a pro forma basis after giving effect to the Advance; (g) the interest reserve adequacy test in Section 4.8 has been satisfied; (h) the equity-first requirement in Section 4.9 has been satisfied; (i) the Borrower has complied with the Borrower's equity funding obligations, if any, and has funded all cost overruns required by Section 4.11; (j) the Intercreditor Agreement remains in full force and effect and no default exists thereunder; (k) the Borrower has complied with all conditions of the NFA Letter applicable as of the date of the Advance, including the restrictions on advances for construction within or above the Restricted Area set forth in Section 6.5(d); and (l) no Material Adverse Effect has occurred.

**Section 4.5 — Retainage.** The Lender shall withhold Retainage equal to ten percent (10%) of the amount of each Advance for hard construction costs. Retainage shall be held by the Lender (or, at the Lender's election, in the Contingency Reserve or a separate retainage escrow) and shall not bear interest for the account of the Borrower. Retainage shall be released only in accordance with Section 4.6. The aggregate Retainage shall equal ten percent (10%) of the GMP, being Three Million Four Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($3,475,000), subject to reduction for Change Orders approved under Section 4.11.

**Section 4.6 — Final Retainage Release.** The Lender shall release the Retainage upon satisfaction of each of the following: (a) Substantial Completion and issuance of the final certificate of occupancy by the City of Durham for all residential units and retail bays; (b) delivery of final, unconditional lien waivers and affidavits from the General Contractor, each subcontractor, and each materialman in statutory form under N.C.G.S. Chapter 44A; (c) delivery of the Architect's certificate of final completion; (d) expiration of the one hundred twenty (120)-day lien filing period under N.C.G.S. Chapter 44A measured from the last furnishing of labor or materials, or delivery of a lien bond or title indemnity satisfactory to the Lender; (e) delivery of as-built drawings, all warranties, guaranties, and operating manuals, and evidence of the installation and performance verification of the soil vapor mitigation system required by the NFA Letter; and (f) confirmation that no mechanic's or materialmen's lien has been filed and that the Title Policy has been endorsed to remove any exception for pending disbursements. If the aggregate Retainage withheld differs from $3,475,000 as a result of Change Orders, the release shall be adjusted accordingly so that the full amount withheld is released.

**Section 4.7 — Interest Reserve Account.** At the Closing, the Lender shall fund the Interest Reserve of $4,850,000 from the Loan proceeds into the Interest Reserve Account, which shall be a segregated sub-account of the Loan. The Interest Reserve Account shall be applied solely to pay interest accruing on the Loan during the Construction Period. On the first Business Day of each calendar month during the Construction Period, the Lender shall apply funds in the Interest Reserve Account to the payment of accrued interest. The Interest Reserve Account is not a trust fund for the benefit of the Borrower, is not a deposit account of the Borrower, and does not reduce the outstanding principal balance of the Loan. Interest shall accrue on the Loan notwithstanding the insufficiency of the Interest Reserve, and the Borrower's obligation to pay interest is absolute.

**Section 4.8 — Interest Reserve Adequacy Test; Replenishment.** (a) At each Draw Request, and in any event not less frequently than quarterly, the Lender shall test the adequacy of the Interest Reserve by comparing the remaining balance of the Interest Reserve Account to the projected interest that will accrue on the Loan from the date of the test through the earlier of (i) the next anticipated draw date and (ii) ninety (90) days after the date of the test, in each case computed at the then-current Applicable Rate on the projected outstanding principal balance. (b) If the projected interest exceeds the remaining balance of the Interest Reserve Account, the Borrower shall deposit cash into the Interest Reserve Account in the amount of the deficiency before the requested Advance will be funded. (c) If at any time the Lender determines that the Interest Reserve is or will be insufficient to pay interest through the end of the Construction Period, the Lender shall notify the Borrower, and the Borrower shall deposit the deficiency into the Interest Reserve Account within five (5) Business Days after written notice. (d) All deposits under this Section 4.8 shall be made from the Borrower's own funds and not from the proceeds of the Loan or the Mezzanine Loan, and shall be evidenced by a certification of the source of funds. Failure to fund any deposit required under this Section 4.8 within the applicable period shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 11.1. (e) The Borrower shall deliver to the Lender, within fifteen (15) days after the end of each calendar month during the Construction Period, a reconciliation of the Interest Reserve Account showing the opening balance, interest charged, deposits, disbursements, and closing balance, together with a projection of remaining interest through the Construction Maturity Date. (f) The Borrower acknowledges that the Interest Reserve has been modeled by the Borrower at an assumed SOFR of 3.50% and the assumption of a twelve-month divisor, whereas the Term Sheet and this Agreement require interest to be computed on actual days elapsed over a 360-day year, and that at prevailing SOFR levels the Interest Reserve is projected to be insufficient. The Borrower's obligations under this Section 4.8 are absolute and are supported by the Carry Guaranty.

**Section 4.9 — Equity First; Equity Escrow Account.** (a) The Borrower's equity, including the Equity Escrow Account, shall be fully invested in the Project before any Advance other than the initial Advance is made. (b) If the Lender requires an equity deposit under Section 3.9, the Lender shall establish the Equity Escrow Account, and the Borrower shall deposit $2,140,000 therein on or before the Closing Date from sources permitted under Section 3.9. Funds in the Equity Escrow Account shall be disbursed by the Lender to fund Project costs (other than those funded by the initial Advance) before any other source is drawn and shall be applied to hard costs and soft costs in the order determined by the Lender. (c) The Borrower shall deliver to the Lender, at Closing and upon each draw, a certification identifying the source of all equity funds and confirming that no equity funds are directly or indirectly derived from the Mezzanine Loan, the Mezzanine Lender, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Thomas R. Chen, or any Affiliate of any of the foregoing, together with bank records and wire confirmations evidencing the source. (d) The Borrower shall not permit any return of, or distribution in respect of, any member's capital contribution during the term of the Loan other than as expressly permitted by Section 7.6.

**Section 4.10 — Contingency Reserve.** The contingency line item in the Approved Budget in the amount of $1,440,000 (comprising $1,140,000 of hard cost contingency and $300,000 of soft cost contingency) shall be funded into the Contingency Reserve at the time provided in **Exhibit D** and shall be disbursed only for Change Orders or cost overruns approved by the Lender in writing. The Borrower shall deliver a change order log with each Draw Request. Upon Substantial Completion, any remaining balance in the Contingency Reserve shall be applied to prepay the outstanding principal balance of the Loan in accordance with Section 2.11 (without payment of any prepayment premium or Exit Fee).

**Section 4.11 — Change Orders; Cost Overruns.** (a) No Change Order may be implemented without the Lender's prior written consent, which the Lender may grant or withhold in its reasonable judgment, and any Change Order (i) that would cause the aggregate amount of all Change Orders to exceed five percent (5%) of the GMP, (ii) that would reduce the scope, quality, or quantity of the Work, (iii) that would extend the construction schedule beyond the Construction Maturity Date, or (iv) that affects any structural, life-safety, envelope, or environmental component of the Work (including the soil vapor mitigation system) requires the Lender's prior written consent in its sole discretion. (b) No Change Order shall increase the GMP unless the Borrower has first deposited into the Contingency Reserve, or otherwise funded from sources other than the Loan and the Mezzanine Loan, the full amount of the increase. (c) All cost overruns shall be funded by the Borrower from equity contributions, Guarantor contributions, or other sources approved by the Lender, and not from Loan proceeds. (d) The Borrower shall deliver to the Lender a certified copy of each executed Change Order within five (5) Business Days after execution, together with the Architect's and Construction Consultant's written evaluation.

**Section 4.12 — No Obligation to Advance; Cancellation.** The Lender shall have no obligation to make any Advance if any condition in this Article IV or Article III has not been satisfied, and no Advance shall constitute a waiver of any condition applicable to a subsequent Advance. If the Borrower fails to satisfy any condition to an Advance for a period of thirty (30) consecutive days after written notice, or if the Work is suspended for a period of thirty (30) consecutive days (other than as a result of a Lender-caused delay), the Lender may, in its sole discretion, cancel the undrawn portion of the Commitment. Any cancellation shall not reduce the Borrower's obligations with respect to amounts already advanced.

**Section 4.13 — Disbursement to Third Parties; No Third-Party Rights.** The Lender may, at its election, disburse Loan proceeds directly to the General Contractor, the Architect, any subcontractor or materialman, the Title Insurer, or any other Person entitled to payment, and any such disbursement shall satisfy the Lender's obligation to advance the corresponding amount to the Borrower. No such Person shall be a third-party beneficiary of this Agreement or have any right to compel any Advance.

**Section 4.14 — Construction Schedule; Delay.** The Borrower shall cause the Work to be performed in accordance with the construction schedule approved by the Lender, which shall provide for Substantial Completion on or before August 31, 2027. If at any time the Construction Consultant determines that the Work is more than ninety (90) days behind the approved construction schedule, an Event of Default shall exist under Section 11.7 without further notice or cure.

EOF

Chapter 44A measured from the last furnishing of labor or materials, or delivery of a lien bond or title indemnity satisfactory to the Lender; (e) delivery of as-built drawings, all warranties, guaranties, and operating manuals, and evidence of the installation and performance verification of the soil vapor mitigation system required by the NFA Letter; and (f) confirmation that no mechanic's or materialmen's lien has been filed and that the Title Policy has been endorsed to remove any exception for pending disbursements. If the aggregate Retainage withheld differs from $3,475,000 as a result of Change Orders, the release shall be adjusted accordingly so that the full amount withheld is released.

**Section 4.7 — Interest Reserve Account.** At the Closing, the Lender shall fund the Interest Reserve of $4,850,000 from the Loan proceeds into the Interest Reserve Account, which shall be a segregated sub-account of the Loan. The Interest Reserve Account shall be applied solely to pay interest accruing on the Loan during the Construction Period. On the first Business Day of each calendar month during the Construction Period, the Lender shall apply funds in the Interest Reserve Account to the payment of accrued interest. The Interest Reserve Account is not a trust fund for the benefit of the Borrower, is not a deposit account of the Borrower, and does not reduce the outstanding principal balance of the Loan. Interest shall accrue on the Loan notwithstanding the insufficiency of the Interest Reserve, and the Borrower's obligation to pay interest is absolute.

**Section 4.8 — Interest Reserve Adequacy Test; Replenishment.** (a) At each Draw Request, and in any event not less frequently than quarterly, the Lender shall test the adequacy of the Interest Reserve by comparing the remaining balance of the Interest Reserve Account to the projected interest that will accrue on the Loan from the date of the test through the earlier of (i) the next anticipated draw date and (ii) ninety (90) days after the date of the test, in each case computed at the then-current Applicable Rate on the projected outstanding principal balance. (b) If the projected interest exceeds the remaining balance of the Interest Reserve Account, the Borrower shall deposit cash into the Interest Reserve Account in the amount of the deficiency before the requested Advance will be funded. (c) If at any time the Lender determines that the Interest Reserve is or will be insufficient to pay interest through the end of the Construction Period, the Lender shall notify the Borrower, and the Borrower shall deposit the deficiency into the Interest Reserve Account within five (5) Business Days after written notice. (d) All deposits under this Section 4.8 shall be made from the Borrower's own funds and not from the proceeds of the Loan or the Mezzanine Loan, and shall be evidenced by a certification of the source of funds. Failure to fund any deposit required under this Section 4.8 within the applicable period shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 11.1. (e) The Borrower shall deliver to the Lender, within fifteen (15) days after the end of each calendar month during the Construction Period, a reconciliation of the Interest Reserve Account showing the opening balance, interest charged, deposits, disbursements, and closing balance, together with a projection of remaining interest through the Construction Maturity Date. (f) The Borrower acknowledges that the Interest Reserve has been modeled by the Borrower at an assumed SOFR of 3.50% and the assumption of a twelve-month divisor, whereas the Term Sheet and this Agreement require interest to be computed on actual days elapsed over a 360-day year, and that at prevailing SOFR levels the Interest Reserve is projected to be insufficient. The Borrower's obligations under this Section 4.8 are absolute and are supported by the Carry Guaranty.

**Section 4.9 — Equity First; Equity Escrow Account.** (a) The Borrower's equity, including the Equity Escrow Account, shall be fully invested in the Project before any Advance other than the initial Advance is made. (b) If the Lender requires an equity deposit under Section 3.9, the Lender shall establish the Equity Escrow Account, and the Borrower shall deposit $2,140,000 therein on or before the Closing Date from sources permitted under Section 3.9. Funds in the Equity Escrow Account shall be disbursed by the Lender to fund Project costs (other than those funded by the initial Advance) before any other source is drawn and shall be applied to hard costs and soft costs in the order determined by the Lender. (c) The Borrower shall deliver to the Lender, at Closing and upon each draw, a certification identifying the source of all equity funds and confirming that no equity funds are directly or indirectly derived from the Mezzanine Loan, the Mezzanine Lender, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Thomas R. Chen, or any Affiliate of any of the foregoing, together with bank records and wire confirmations evidencing the source. (d) The Borrower shall not permit any return of, or distribution in respect of, any member's capital contribution during the term of the Loan other than as expressly permitted by Section 7.6.

**Section 4.10 — Contingency Reserve.** The contingency line item in the Approved Budget in the amount of $1,440,000 (comprising $1,140,000 of hard cost contingency and $300,000 of soft cost contingency) shall be funded into the Contingency Reserve at the time provided in **Exhibit D** and shall be disbursed only for Change Orders or cost overruns approved by the Lender in writing. The Borrower shall deliver a change order log with each Draw Request. Upon Substantial Completion, any remaining balance in the Contingency Reserve shall be applied to prepay the outstanding principal balance of the Loan in accordance with Section 2.11 (without payment of any prepayment premium or Exit Fee).

**Section 4.11 — Change Orders; Cost Overruns.** (a) No Change Order may be implemented without the Lender's prior written consent, which the Lender may grant or withhold in its reasonable judgment, and any Change Order (i) that would cause the aggregate amount of all Change Orders to exceed five percent (5%) of the GMP, (ii) that would reduce the scope, quality, or quantity of the Work, (iii) that would extend the construction schedule beyond the Construction Maturity Date, or (iv) that affects any structural, life-safety, envelope, or environmental component of the Work (including the soil vapor mitigation system) requires the Lender's prior written consent in its sole discretion. (b) No Change Order shall increase the GMP unless the Borrower has first deposited into the Contingency Reserve, or otherwise funded from sources other than the Loan and the Mezzanine Loan, the full amount of the increase. (c) All cost overruns shall be funded by the Borrower from equity contributions, Guarantor contributions, or other sources approved by the Lender, and not from Loan proceeds. (d) The Borrower shall deliver to the Lender a certified copy of each executed Change Order within five (5) Business Days after execution, together with the Architect's and Construction Consultant's written evaluation.

**Section 4.12 — No Obligation to Advance; Cancellation.** The Lender shall have no obligation to make any Advance if any condition in this Article IV or Article III has not been satisfied, and no Advance shall constitute a waiver of any condition applicable to a subsequent Advance. If the Borrower fails to satisfy any condition to an Advance for a period of thirty (30) consecutive days after written notice, or if the Work is suspended for a period of thirty (30) consecutive days (other than as a result of a Lender-caused delay), the Lender may, in its sole discretion, cancel the undrawn portion of the Commitment. Any cancellation shall not reduce the Borrower's obligations with respect to amounts already advanced.

**Section 4.13 — Disbursement to Third Parties; No Third-Party Rights.** The Lender may, at its election, disburse Loan proceeds directly to the General Contractor, the Architect, any subcontractor or materialman, the Title Insurer, or any other Person entitled to payment, and any such disbursement shall satisfy the Lender's obligation to advance the corresponding amount to the Borrower. No such Person shall be a third-party beneficiary of this Agreement or have any right to compel any Advance.

**Section 4.14 — Construction Schedule; Delay.** The Borrower shall cause the Work to be performed in accordance with the construction schedule approved by the Lender, which shall provide for Substantial Completion on or before August 31, 2027. If at any time the Construction Consultant determines that the Work is more than ninety (90) days behind the approved construction schedule, an Event of Default shall exist under Section 11.7 without further notice or cure.

**Section 5.7 — No Default.** No Default or Event of Default exists under any Loan Document, the Mezzanine Documents, the Intercreditor Agreement, or any other material agreement to which the Borrower or any Guarantor is a party.

**Section 5.8 — Compliance with Laws; Zoning; Permits.** The Property and the Project comply in all material respects with all applicable laws, ordinances, rules, regulations, and zoning requirements, including the MU-D zoning classification under the City of Durham Unified Development Ordinance and the Declaration recorded in Book 6984, Page 1155, Durham County Registry. The Project is permitted as of right, and no variance, special use permit, conditional zoning, or rezoning is required. All permits, licenses, and approvals necessary for the construction of the Project have been obtained or will be obtained prior to the commencement of the applicable phase of the Work.

**Section 5.9 — Environmental Representations.** (a) Except for the residual petroleum contamination described in the Phase I ESA and the Phase II ESA and addressed by the NFA Letter, there are no Hazardous Materials in, on, under, or migrating from the Property in quantities requiring investigation, remediation, or reporting under any Environmental Law, and the Property is not subject to any Environmental Claim or any outstanding order, directive, or notice of violation.
